### [spec.1.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: `resuming` is not adopted; SPEC-2a gains one sentence pointing at the §6.2 `resuming` watchdog evaluated from the session row — BECAUSE excluding it keeps `coordination_generation` fixed for the whole of a driver's `resuming` window (only adoption and the terminal collapse bump it), which makes a generation condition on the driver's row writes sufficient fencing — ALTERNATIVES: adopting `resuming` (adopter inherits a half-claimed pod held by a dead attempt, and the generation can change mid-restore, so the commit needs more than a guard).
DECISION: SPEC-1b fencing is a generation condition on every driver row write (the `resuming` write and the `running` commit), stated once in the attempt preamble; no fence-at-claim is added — BECAUSE the replacement pod was never addressed by another coordinator, and §10.1.2 step 3 already lets a pod with no fenced generation accept the session's RPCs — ALTERNATIVES: reviewer's "send CoordinatorFence before the first operational RPC" (unneeded once the writes are conditional, and conflicts with CODE-4 item 4 / summary Watch-out on fencing after the commit).
WATCHOUT: the guard on the `resuming` write alone is not enough. A stale driver A in `resuming` with a lapsed lease can have its row returned to `resume_pending` by the watchdog, adopted by B, and moved to `resuming` again by B's driver; A's commit guarded only on `State == resuming` then passes. The commit needs the generation condition too — EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-4 item 5.2 (state-only guard); pkg/gateway/runtime/watchdog/watchdog.go sweepResuming (row scan, RetryCount++).

WATCHOUT: summary.md rejected-alternatives line "A generation-guarded commit with publish-after-commit plus a lock..." reads as rejecting the commit guard this design adds; reword it in the same edit.
OPEN: CODE-4 item 3.3 lets a driver take a lapsed lease with a plain `acquireCoordinationLease` and no `RecordHandoff` when both A's and B's leases lapsed; the attempt's generation read at item 3.1 then passes. Narrow, pre-existing in the draft, not filed.

### [spec.1.fix-design-G5.1]
DECISION: the SPEC-5o re-arm fires when a root with a delegation tree enters `suspended` as well as when it leaves. Because the TTL is re-armed to its full value at entry and has to exceed `gateway.maxSuspendedSessionSeconds`, it cannot run out during a suspension that started with a successful re-arm. SPEC-5o is the one home for the re-arm rule and for the residual (a root out of `suspended` longer than the TTL meets BUDGET_KEYS_EXPIRED). SPEC-5g and the Edge-cases bullet point to it. BECAUSE re-arming only on leave left TTL minus the non-suspended time since the last arm at suspension entry, and that can fall below the 7 d lifetime. ALTERNATIVES: a sliding TTL refreshed by budget_reserve/return.lua (rejected: a tree with no delegation operations for longer than the TTL still expires, and it changes the Lua contract); re-arm on entry only (rejected: the cycling awaiting_client_action/resume_pending case would get about 1 d instead of 8 d); re-arm on every state transition (rejected: more Redis writes for no extra guarantee).
FACT: the observable outcome of a TTL expiry (root goes to `failed`) is already stated in §8.3 **`BUDGET_KEYS_EXPIRED` detection and tree cleanup.** item 3 and in the §6.2/§7.2 `suspended → failed` state-machine rows, so the §6.2 sentence that SPEC-5g deletes does not need restoring. EVIDENCE: spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:414, spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:216

OPEN: SPEC-5o re-arms only the root's tree-wide budget keys, while §8.3 sets the TTL on "all delegation budget keys" (per-child keys included). OPEN: Budget-key TTL re-arm only on leaving `suspended` plus "TTL must exceed lifetime" does not stop the TTL firing during a later suspension when non-suspended time since the last re-arm exceeds TTL − lifetime; re-arming on entry to `suspended` closes it.

### [spec.1.review-performance.1]
FACT: Top-tier capacity numbers for lease math: Tier 3 = 10,000 concurrent sessions, 200 creations/s (spec/16_observability.md:595-597); lease renewal row ~1,000/s, total Redis writes ~6,500/s (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:266-268); Coordination Redis role described as "low throughput, small key space" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:253); Postgres sustained write IOPS ~1,300/s, burst ~3,900/s at Tier 3 (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:70, spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1176-1177); REG-COORDLEASE TTL 60 s (spec/28_communication-channels.md:137). EVIDENCE: as cited.
FACT: In the shipped tree no podless suspended row exists and every non-terminal row is expired 7200 s after creation (pkg/gateway/runtime/watchdog/watchdog.go:1084 `now.Sub(row.CreatedAt)`), and the coordination Sweeper never adopts a suspended session (pkg/gateway/coordination/coordination/coordination.go:262 isRunningPod). So SPEC-2a + SPEC-5g create a new population of 7-day podless suspended sessions that hold and renew REG-COORDLEASE. EVIDENCE: as cited.
WATCHOUT: The Sweeper upserts the REG-COORDMIRROR Postgres row for every held lease on every sweep (coordination.go:503 upsertMirror), so every lease the spec makes a replica hold is also a periodic Postgres write in the tree. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/coordination/coordination/coordination.go:503,632.
DECISION: Filed one finding: SPEC-2a lease retention in podless `suspended` scales Redis renewals, Postgres-fallback renewals, and crash/rolling-update adoptions with the 7-day suspended population — BECAUSE abandoned sessions now live 604800 s rather than 7200 s — ALTERNATIVES: filing checkpoint/MinIO load of idle suspension (rejected: shipped sessions already export a final snapshot and pods are held no longer than under shipped idle expiry), resume-driver retry cadence (rejected: claim rate is bounded by client resumes, speculative).

DECISION: security lens filed no findings on the spec staging — BECAUSE the controls it touches stay intact: pin-read failure on resume still claims no pod (SPEC-3h), BUDGET_KEYS_EXPIRED still fails the tree closed (spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:408-417, not edited), cross-tenant send validation covers all message paths (spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:277), and the idle release takes the pool's session-end disposition (recycle runs credential purge and whole-pod scrub, spec/05_runtime-registry-and-pool-model.md:480) — ALTERNATIVES: filing "no turn in flight" as a pod self-report was rejected because the idle bound is resource reclamation and maxSessionAge still caps a pod that never ends its turn; "any message resumes, including a sibling's queued send" is an owner decision.

UNVERIFIED: whether the SPEC-1b item 2 `resume_pending → resuming` write must be conditioned on the driver's coordination_generation so that a replica whose lease lapsed cannot win it after a peer adopts. §10.1.5 implies session-row writes are generation-CAS'd (spec/10_gateway-internals.md §10.1.5 "failed Postgres CAS on the session row"), but SPEC-1b does not say so. ### [spec.2.fix-design-G2.1]
DECISION: Pre-suspension inbox entries are delivered by the resume driver, which runs on the coordinating replica that holds the default-mode in-memory inbox. SPEC-1b item 4 (§7.3 **Resume driver.**) is the one home: it delivers session-inbox entries, then the entries buffered while recovering. CODE-4 item 6 `DrainForResume` reads the session inbox through `Coordinator.inbox` in both modes, not only the durable inbox — BECAUSE the coordinator keeps the in-memory inbox through a podless suspension, and `Coordinator.inbox` is the in-memory store or the Redis list depending on the mode — ALTERNATIVES: draining the inbox to the DLQ when the pod is released (SPEC-5b step 2) was rejected because DLQ entries are scored by expiry at now + maxResumeWindowSeconds and would expire during a suspension that can last 7 days. Restoring the §7.2 inbox-to-DLQ drain inside path 6 was rejected because the serving replica cannot reach the coordinator's inbox (see the [spec.1.fix-G3.1] WATCHOUT).
FACT: FIFO holds in both serving cases. When the coordinator serves the podless transition, `enterResumePending` → `migrateInboxOnResumePending` moves the inbox into the DLQ before CODE-6 item 7's `bufferTargetDLQ`, so the DLQ score order is already FIFO. When a non-coordinator serves it, that replica's drain is a no-op, and the coordinator's inbox entries, which are older, come before the DLQ. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/messaging.go:112; pkg/gateway/session/sessioninbox/coordinator.go:104 (MigrateInboxToDLQ drains c.inbox and enqueues to the DLQ with DefaultDLQTTL); non-spec-changes.md CODE-4 item 9, CODE-6 item 7.
DECISION: SPEC-5b gains no "release leaves the inbox in place" sentence. Nothing states that the release clears the inbox. In default mode, a coordinator crash during suspension or recovery loses the in-memory inbox under the existing guarantee at spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:314 ("does not drop ... while the coordinating replica remains alive").
FACT: Despite its name, `clearInboxOnResume` / `ClearInboxOnAcquire` clears nothing. It emits only `inbox_cleared` with the DLQ length. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/session/sessioninbox/coordinator.go:232-248.
OPEN: CODE-4 item 5.5 moves `clearInboxOnResume` into the driver's tail unchanged. In default mode the driver then emits `inbox_cleared` with reason `coordinator_failover` on every restore, including restores where no failover happened and the driver is about to deliver the inbox. This existed before the move, in handleResume, and is a separate finding for a later round.

CODE-4 defers PodAssignment until the commit, so the driver's claimed pod is unreferenced for up to the whole `resuming` window. Today the watchdog cancels the attempt before the orphan GC can drain it. Raising MaxResumingSeconds above claimOrphanTimeout would let the GC drain a pod mid-restore. Not filed, because it is a code choice.

### [spec.5.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: SPEC-1b's attempt write condition is the row's state as the attempt last read or wrote it plus an unchanged `coordination_generation`, with at most one attempt per session and each attempt ending by the `resuming` watchdog's deadline — BECAUSE the §6.2 `resuming` watchdog returns the row to `resume_pending` without bumping the generation (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:241; only adoption and snapshot-close bump), so a generation-only guard let an overtaken attempt and a fresh one both commit — ALTERNATIVES: a watchdog exception clause (each later overtaking write needs another), a state-only CAS (ABA when attempt B rewrites `resuming`), having the watchdog bump the generation (changes landed 0091 semantics), copying CODE-4's in-flight set and timer into the spec (mechanism belongs to CODE-4).
WATCHOUT: SPEC-1b item 2 no longer carries its own "left `resume_pending` by then, release and stop" sentence; the lead write condition covers it. Do not reinstate it, and do not renumber items 1-4 (SPEC-3o cites items 1 and 2, SPEC-3p cites item 4). Pointers that named "item 2" for the release (SPEC-1e item 4, edge case **Terminate or cancel racing the driver.**) now name the paragraph.

### [spec.5.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: SPEC-1b's write condition becomes a compare-and-swap on the state the attempt last read or wrote plus the unchanged coordination_generation, with "at most one attempt per session at a time, ending no later than the `resuming` watchdog's deadline" — BECAUSE the watchdog moves `resuming → resume_pending` without a generation bump, and a state-only CAS has an ABA hole (B rewrites `resuming` before A commits) that only the one-attempt bound closes — ALTERNATIVES: generation-only guard (the failed predicate); state-only CAS (ABA); bump the generation on the watchdog write (changes §6.2 and the 0091 generation semantics for a non-adoption edge).
DECISION: item 2's "When the session row has left `resume_pending` by then, the driver releases the claimed pod and stops" is deleted as a restatement of the lead condition; SPEC-1e item 4 and the **Terminate or cancel racing the driver.** edge case retarget from "item 2" to **Resume driver.**; SPEC-3o "items 1 and 2" stays (item numbering unchanged).
FACT: CODE-4 already implements the new condition: in-flight set (item 2), deadline reset to MaxResumingSeconds (item 3.4), hook guard State==resume_pending+gen (3.4), commit guard State==resuming+gen with pod release (5.2-5.3), failure report gen-guarded and routed by state (3.7). No non-spec change needed — EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-4 items 2, 3.4, 3.7, 5.2-5.3
FACT: the `resuming` watchdog write carries no generation bump; only the terminal snapshot-close and adoption bump it — EVIDENCE: spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:241, spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:221

### [spec.5.review-reliability.1]
DECISION: Returned no findings for the staged spec edits under the reliability lens — BECAUSE every recovery path traced (driver crash before and after the claim, watchdog-vs-attempt race on one replica, podless adoption without a fence, suspension release crash, budget-key re-arm) either serializes on the session row or falls to an existing reclaimer (§4.6.1 claim GC predicate 1, §6.2 `resuming` watchdog) — ALTERNATIVES: filing the narrow windows below as spec findings (their remedies are code, or they repeat refuted materiality cases).
FACT: A replacement pod is not named in `pod_assignment` during `resuming` in the current tree either: `bumpRecoveryGeneration` (the PodAssignment write) runs after `binder.Resume` returns. So CODE-4 moving it to the commit adds no new claim-GC exposure. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/resume_rebind.go:129; spec/04_system-components.md:517.
FACT: Same-replica attempt overlap is safe at row level. A watchdog `resuming → resume_pending` does not bump `coordination_generation`, but the `running` commit guard on `State == resuming` serializes a stale attempt against a fresh one, and the loser releases its pod. EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md SPEC-1b preamble; non-spec-changes.md CODE-4 item 5.2.
FACT: `resume_pending` rows keep the failed pod in `PodAssignment` by design (the failure reporters stamp it), so "no bound pod" in SPEC-2b has to be read as "binding released" per §28.5.1 CH-ATTACH, not as an empty column. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/failure.go:337-338; spec/28_communication-channels.md:261.
UNVERIFIED: The CODE-6 `SuspendIdle` turn check and guarded write do not take the per-session delivery lock. A message classified `running` just before the write can start a turn on a pod that the next tick checkpoints and releases. The tier-7a test claims it never loses the message, but no mechanism is staged. The non-spec loop should check whether message delivery stamps `LastAgentActivityAt` before it sends. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 5; pkg/gateway/session/sessionidle/sessionidle.go:234.
UNVERIFIED: The podless message branch writes `resume_pending` and then enqueues to the DLQ (CODE-6 item 7). A driver that restores and drains before the enqueue strands the message in the DLQ of a `running` session. The window is tiny, so the non-spec loop should decide whether to enqueue first.
UNVERIFIED: The CODE-4 lease gate treats a lease read error as "not holder". During a Redis outage this stops every resume driver, while spec/12_storage-architecture.md:217 says leases fall back to Postgres. The non-spec loop owns this.

DECISION: Resume-attempt supersession was redesigned — BECAUSE the 2026-10-07 run stopped on an ABA-prone SPEC-1b write condition. The `resume_pending → resuming` write now increments `coordination_generation` (SPEC-1b, SPEC-1f for §4.2 and §10.1.1, CODE-4 item 3.4), every exit from `resuming` is conditioned on that incarnation (SPEC-1b **Exits from `resuming`.**, CODE-4 items 3.7 and 5.2), the resumed binding is stamped with the post-entry generation (CODE-4 item 5.4), and the attempt that claimed the replacement pod is its only releaser (CODE-4 item 5.3).
DECISION: The `resuming` watchdog was redesigned — BECAUSE `sweepResuming` wrote the row on a state miss, took the retry branch from the listed row, and counted a report-produced `resume_pending` row as a watchdog retry. Its exit is now guarded on the listed row's generation, computes the retry branch from the locked row, and returns `errResumingSuperseded` on a miss (CODE-4 item 15).
DECISION: The parked residue of a `suspended` session was redesigned — BECAUSE a held-pod resume fault and an off-holder fallback buffered into a replica-local inbox no coordinator reads. Every undelivered message to a `suspended` session now waits in the session's DLQ (SPEC-5i, SPEC-5l, CODE-6 items 6, 7, and 12), `deliverBuffered` sweeps expired entries before it drains (CODE-4 item 6), and SPEC-5z widens the `dlq_ttl_expired` definitions and the terminal DLQ drain to a `suspended` target.

### [redesign.2]
FACT: Redesign 1 of the 2026-10-08 redesign run (scratchpad/redesign/0092_new_write-the-session-suspend-and-resume-proposal-that-gateway-redesign-1.md) was applied on 2026-10-08. Every anchor matched once, and no edit was skipped. Its commentary sentences after edit 7a, after edit 19 ("SPEC-5q edits other rows of §16.1. The two edits do not overlap."), and in edit 16 (withdrawn) were not inserted.
DECISION: Message custody across suspend and resume was redesigned — BECAUSE the 2026-10-08 run stopped on a held message that could be both forwarded and enqueued, a drain that wrote back to a per-replica inbox, and an enqueue that could land after the drain. SPEC-5i delivery path 6 is now the one home of custody: synchronous delivery only for a REST message the coordinating replica serves while the row names a pod, every other message held in the DLQ before any state write, a backlog resume by the coordinating replica's suspended sweep (CODE-6 item 2), the `holdMessage` re-read and all-or-nothing removal (CODE-4 item 7), a `deliverBuffered` that pops one DLQ entry at a time and restores the unattempted ones (CODE-4 item 6), an unconditional per-session delivery lock on both message paths, and `resuming` added to the recovering states (SPEC-5z items 2 to 6, CODE-6 item 7).
DECISION: Idle suspension was made atomic with a turn — BECAUSE no delivery stamps `LastAgentActivityAt`, `Stamp` is asynchronous, and the turn token is free between turns of one batch. `PodExecutor.Send` makes the synchronous `StampSync` admission write and refuses a `suspended` row, `TurnInFlight` covers the whole `Send`, and a refused batch is routed again (SPEC-5f, CODE-6 items 5 and 7).
DECISION: The readers of `coordination_generation` were reconciled with the entry increment — BECAUSE `peerTookOver` read a per-replica record that goes stale across a same-replica rebind and `RecordHandoff` incremented unconditionally. CODE-5 items 2a and 2b compare against the binding stamp and make `RecordHandoff` a compare-and-swap; SPEC-1f items 5 and 6 reword the §7.1 and §16.1 derive-failure fence; SPEC-1f item 3 adds the §10.1.5 **Session with no bound pod.** paragraph; CODE-4 item 17 rewrites the `derive.go` comments; and the barrier generation lag is RECORDS-1 finding 7(h).
DECISION: An off-holder `POST /resume` of a held-pod `suspended` session fails closed with `TARGET_NOT_READY` (CODE-4 item 8), because a drain off the lease holder fails every `Send` in `streamFor`. RECORDS-1 finding 7(b) records the missing forward.

DECISION: A DLQ entry left in a `running` session's DLQ (stopped drain, failed re-read) is an accepted outcome stated once in path 6 **Delivery after a commit to `running`.**; RECORDS-1 7(g) and the summary Defects entry are deleted because the tree then conforms — ALTERNATIVES: a drain on lease takeover of a `running` session, or a `running`-row DLQ sweep (new mechanism; rejected in standing context for cost).

Owner: the §7.2 path 6 / suspension-release area.

DECISION: Filed two failure-mode findings. (1) The SPEC-5f admission write makes Postgres a synchronous dependency of every message delivery, and the staged text states no outcome when that write fails. §12.3 says existing sessions continue through a failover of up to 30 s, and CODE-6 item 5.2 fails `Send` on any admitter error. (2) SPEC-5i makes the Redis DLQ the only custody for undelivered `suspended`-target messages and puts a DLQ drain in front of synchronous held-pod delivery, but states no outcome for a failed enqueue or drain read. The receipt enum's `inbox_unavailable` is scoped to `durableInbox: true`. — BECAUSE each one is a store outage that degrades below the shipped behavior, with no outcome stated in the staged spec — ALTERNATIVES: suspended-population scaling (refuted earlier); the cost of the admission write (OD-A is open).
FACT: CODE-6 item 5.2 has `Send` return the admitter's error and write no envelope. A Postgres failover therefore fails every message delivery to every running session, on every replica. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md:134; spec/12_storage-architecture.md:153

### [spec.2.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: The SPEC-5i path 6 drain restores the failed DLQ entry with the unattempted ones at their original scores, so the DLQ half is at-least-once like the inbox half — BECAUSE a dropped entry after an ambiguous pod or stream failure is lost with no `message_expired`, breaking the §7.2 promise to senders holding `queued` (spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:350, :352) — ALTERNATIVES: at-most-once plus `message_expired` (no legal reason value; notifies a loss the restore avoids), per-error-kind exceptions (the removed `ErrSessionSuspended` branch), a `delivered_message_ids` clause in the staged text (defends rather than instructs; no adapter code implements the set).
WATCHOUT: Replaced: "A drained DLQ entry is delivered at most once" with the idle-refusal-only restore exception (`TestDeliverBufferedRestoresRefusedEntry`, CODE-6 item 5.4's `deliverBuffered` sentence). It lost because the common post-resume failure (pod failure or stream break) dropped the entry with no sender notification. Do not reintroduce an error-kind branch in `deliverBuffered`; redelivery duplicates are the adapter's `delivered_message_ids` concern (spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:305).
DECISION: `dlq_ttl_expired` carries no state predicate ("pre-terminal DLQ TTL elapsed before the message was delivered") in §7.2 and §15.4 — BECAUSE a restored entry can expire in a `running` session's DLQ, and the pre-running DLQ row (spec/07:348) also expires entries; a state list drifts each time custody gains a state and the enum is closed (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1641) — ALTERNATIVES: adding `running` to the list, sweeping `running` rows in `sweepDLQExpiry` (a Redis call per running row per tick).
DECISION: The dead-letter recovering-state row's "delivered in FIFO order" sentence is replaced by a pointer at path 6 **Delivery after a commit to `running`.** (SPEC-5z item 4) — BECAUSE the DLQ is scored by expiry, so FIFO and score order disagree when TTLs differ; path 6 is the one home of drain order.
CORRECTS [DECISION SPEC-5z widens ... to a `suspended` target]: SPEC-5z no longer widens `dlq_ttl_expired` to `suspended`; it removes the state predicate. The §7.3 terminal DLQ drain bullet (item 2) still names `suspended`.

### [spec.2.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: A drained DLQ entry whose delivery fails is returned to the DLQ at its score whatever the failure, so the DLQ drain is at-least-once like the inbox half of the same drain (durable-inbox Explicit ACK row) — BECAUSE dropping it loses a `queued` message with no `message_expired` under the pod or stream failure the drain most often meets, and the refusal exception becomes unnecessary — ALTERNATIVES: keep at-most-once and emit `message_expired` for the dropped entry (needs a fourth enum value; the enum is closed); keep the idle-refusal exception (hair: an error-kind branch the uniform rule makes redundant).
DECISION: `dlq_ttl_expired` is redefined state-independently ("pre-terminal DLQ TTL elapsed before the message was delivered") — BECAUSE a returned entry can expire in a `running` session's DLQ and the drain expires it; listing states again would drift from path 6. This also gives the pre-running DLQ row's expiry a legal reason.
DECISION: The dead-letter recovering-state row's "delivered in FIFO order" sentence is replaced by a pointer to path 6 **Delivery after a commit to `running`.**, the one home of drain order (score order).
CORRECTS [Standing context DECISION "SPEC-5z widens the §7.2 and §15.4 `dlq_ttl_expired` definitions ... to a `suspended` target"]: after this round the two definitions name no state; only the §7.3 terminal-drain bullet (SPEC-5z item 2) and the Target-state cells widen.

SPEC-1b **Exits from `resuming`.**, CODE-4 item 5.3, summary decision 15, and the shutdown edge case name the §4.6.1 orphan-claim GC as the second releaser of a stopped attempt's pod and accept its drain of a restore older than `claimOrphanTimeout`; CODE-4 item 19 adds the `--max-resuming-seconds` help — BECAUSE the attempt was stated as the only releaser while the GC already reclaims the pod, and the two binaries cannot enforce an ordering of their timeouts.

SPEC-1b's "No session's `pod_assignment` names that pod" therefore holds on concurrent-workspace pools too, and the WPC orphan GC predicate 1 can select it. SandboxClaim spec and status stay gateway-owned (spec/04_system-components.md §4.6.3 table), REG-COORDLEASE is a Redis lease rather than a Kubernetes Lease (spec/28_communication-channels.md:137), and every new state edge is a Postgres row write. The Kubernetes-idiom lens found nothing in round 1.

Between those two writes the claim is still `bound` with an old transition time and no session references it, so a WPC GC tick can drain a pod the gateway is about to recycle. The outcome fails closed (a drain), and it is the GC lookup-then-drain race the Standing context already records as predating this proposal. Do not file it as a new defect. ### [spec.1.review-performance.1]
USEFUL [spec.1.review-performance.1 WATCHOUT, 7-day suspended population]: it saved re-deriving and re-filing lease-renewal and backlog-probe scaling. For the record, the math is Tier 3 claim rate 30/s (spec/16_observability.md:609) × abandoned fraction f × 604800 s. That gives about 18M·f suspended rows, each with a REG-COORDLEASE renewal every 30 s and a DLQ ZCOUNT every 5 s watchdog tick. The family is still refuted as a design choice that no spec-stated population bound contradicts.
FACT: Redesign 3 puts a DLQ peek (Redis ZRANGE) in front of every path-2 delivery (SPEC-5i **Delivery of held messages.**; non-spec-changes.md CODE-4 item 6 "Callers"). A `Peek` error stops the loop (non-spec-changes.md:86). During a Redis outage, a path-2 message to a `running` session in default inbox mode is therefore queued in the inbox rather than delivered, until Redis returns. Not filed: it is the same degraded-mode family the redesign2 skeptic refuted (scratchpad/cp-log/0092-redesign2/history/spec.r2.history.md:25), no message is lost, and the shipped rate limiter already fails closed after 60 s of Redis outage (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:216, :232). A Redis lens that wants to reopen it needs a loss case or a spec contradiction, not a latency case.
FACT: The SPEC-5f admission-write failover finding was refuted in redesign2 (spec.r2.history.md:24). The skeptic's reason was that message paths already `store.Get` the row (messages.go:213), and that §12.3's "writes requiring Postgres ... are rejected" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:153) covers it. Do not refile it.
DECISION: Returned no findings — BECAUSE every per-unit-of-work write the staged spec adds is either a Postgres row write already required per qualifying event (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:265), the OD-A open cost, or a Redis op whose population scaling was refuted earlier. Postgres failover, Redis reset, and coordinator handoff leave `coordination_generation`, `retryCount`, and the DLQ entries no worse than shipped. Held messages are at-least-once across a handoff, and the duplicate is acknowledged in SPEC-5i — ALTERNATIVES: filing the head-of-line latency of delivering held messages before each path-2 message (rejected: it is redesign 3's owner-approved design, and a preference rather than a defect); filing the idle suspend/backlog-resume pod-restore loop for an undeliverable held entry (rejected: maxSessionAge active time bounds it to about 8 cycles, and no deterministic Send failure was shown).

### [spec.4.review-mechanism.1]
FACT: The code keeps `PodAssignment` on a row that enters `resume_pending` (failure.go:337-338, :379-380, :424-425 copy the reporter's pod in), so a recovering row can name a dead pod. SPEC-2b's "no bound pod" therefore has to be read from state as well as `pod_assignment`; CODE-5's predicate treats `resume_pending` and `awaiting_client_action` as podless whatever the column holds (non-spec-changes.md:272). DECISION: Did not file the SPEC-5f clause "a delivery refused after that write ... routes it by §7.2 delivery path 6" as a conflict with the **Delivery of held messages.** failure rule ("the entry stays at the head of its queue") for a refused held entry — BECAUSE the worst reading re-enqueues a copy, and a duplicate is inside the at-least-once guarantee, so nothing becomes inconsistent or broken. CODE-6 item 7 re-routes only the new batch, and `deliverBuffered` leaves the held entry where it is (non-spec-changes.md:86, :155).
DEFERRED [non-spec-changes.md]: CODE-6 item 7 (`ResumeSuspended`, line 158) says that when the row names a pod and the lease gate refuses this replica, "the coordinating replica's backlog resume (item 2) resumes the session". A backlog resume fires only on held messages, and for an interrupt suspension only on DLQ entries accepted after `SuspendedAt`. If any caller sends a message-less `resume_session` there, the claim is false and the call is silently dropped. The fix: fail closed as the REST `/resume` held-pod off-holder branch does (TARGET_NOT_READY, CODE-4 item 8), or confirm that only message paths call `ResumeSuspended` and say so.

DECISION: Returned no findings in spec round 7 — BECAUSE the only change since the r5 snapshot is the SPEC-1b **Retry accounting.** sentence ("No other entry into `resume_pending` advances it."), which adds no write and no store dependency. EVIDENCE: spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:236; spec-changes.md SPEC-5b step 2

### [spec.7.review-reliability.1]
DECISION: Returned no findings under the reliability lens for round 7 — BECAUSE every traced message edge either delivers at least once with removal after `Send` or expires through the recovering-state sweep. The edges traced were idle suspension with zero-hold release racing a coordinator-held message, podless and held-pod resume on and off the coordinator, a coordinator crash after a `running` commit and before held delivery (picked up by the next path-2 delivery or by idle suspension plus **Backlog resume.**), a serving-replica crash between DLQ enqueue and the state write (**Backlog resume.**), and an enqueue racing a terminal transition. Driver crash before the claim, before entry, and after the claim end in the `resuming` watchdog or the §4.6.1 predicate-1 claim GC. The coordination_generation progression has one home (§10.1.1 via SPEC-1f item 2) — ALTERNATIVES: refiling Redis- or Postgres-outage stalls of path-2 delivery (the DLQ peek and the admission write). The redesign2 history refuted both (spec.r2.history.md, the admission-write and DLQ-custody entries), and review-log FACT at :871 records the peek case.
FACT: Partial-manifest selection on resume uses MAX(coordination_generation) over the session's manifests (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:171). The entry increment in SPEC-1b leaves it intact because no manifest is written during `resuming` and every later checkpoint is stamped with a generation at least as high — EVIDENCE: spec/10_gateway-internals.md:153,157,171

### [spec.9.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: SPEC-5f **Idle suspension.** no longer gives an outcome for a refused held-message delivery; it points to §7.2 **Delivery of held messages.** (SPEC-5i), which is the one home for a failed held delivery (entry stays at its queue head), and routes any other refused message again by the session's then-current state — BECAUSE a held delivery is covered by the admission write and SuspendIdle runs without the delivery lock, so the old "route it by path 6" re-enqueued a held entry (duplicate inbox copy, re-scored DLQ entry) — ALTERNATIVES: reviewer's "held stays held, other by path 6" (hard-coded path 6 is wrong once a resume commits `running` before the re-route, and diverges from **Synchronous delivery.** and CODE-6 item 7); deleting the clause (refused non-held path-2 message would have no stated outcome).
WATCHOUT: Never route a refused held entry (inbox or DLQ) by path 6 or re-enqueue it; that duplicates inbox entries and breaks DLQ acceptance order. — EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md SPEC-5i **Delivery of held messages.** "the entry stays at the head of its queue"

### [spec.9.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: SPEC-5f **Idle suspension.** stops stating where a refused held message goes; it says a refused held message stays held, citing **Delivery of held messages.** (SPEC-5i) as the home, and routes any other refused message again by the state the session is then in. BECAUSE the failure outcome of a held delivery already has one home (SPEC-5i "When the delivery of a held message fails, the replica stops and the entry stays at the head of its queue"), and "route by the state then in" is what CODE-6 item 7 builds (re-classify the fresh row) and what **Synchronous delivery.** already says. ALTERNATIVES: deleting the SPEC-5f clause outright leaves a refused non-held path-2 message (no held entries ahead of it) with no stated outcome, because path 2 itself only defines the timeout fallthrough to path 5; keeping "routes it by path 6" for non-held messages is wrong if a resume wrote `running` before the re-route.
FACT: a path-2 Send cannot be refused after a successful held delivery in the same pass, because the held delivery's StampSync advances last_agent_activity_at and the suspension write is guarded on it unchanged; the only refused new-message case is when no held entry was delivered first. EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md SPEC-5f **Idle suspension.**; non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 5.1 StampSync.
WATCHOUT: summary item 16 says "a refused batch is routed by §7.2 delivery path 6"; "batch" there is the new message, so it stays true and was left alone. Do not extend it to held entries.

### [non-spec.1.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: Close the Resume hook-error release (finding "slot-pool Resume deletes the shared SandboxClaim") and CODE-4 item 5.3 (failResume does not delete the claim) with ONE helper change: `releaseResumeSlot` deletes the claim with `podclaim.DeleteClaim` when the slot ID is empty, and keeps the reservation release on a slot pool (whose occupancy-zero edge deletes the claim). The Resume hook-error release becomes `cl.Close` + `releaseResumeSlot(leaked=false)`; item 5.3 cites `failResume`, which already calls it after the pod-side reclaim — BECAUSE the per-pool-kind rule then has one home (the helper) and both callers inherit it — ALTERNATIVES: the reviewers' per-site conditional ("DeleteClaim on exclusive, releaseResumeSlot on slot") written into both the CODE-3 Resume bullet and item 5.3 (rejected: the same predicate stated twice, and an implementor of 5.3 still adds a DeleteClaim beside failResume); calling `Binder.Release`/`rollbackBinding` for 5.3 (rejected: release.go:66 `releaseCredentials(result.SessionID)` revokes every session lease, the scope defect of finding 1).
FACT: `failResume` on an exclusive pool today leaves the claim in place: `releaseResumeSlot` returns nil for an empty slot ID and nothing in `accountResumeSlotFailure` (slot_bind.go) deletes it, so a failed adapter Resume on an exclusive pool leaks the claim to orphan GC. The helper change fixes that path too. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/resume.go:274-297; pkg/gateway/sessionserver/slot_bind.go:452-457
FACT: `Binder.Bind` = `Claim` → `Prepare` → `Launch`; credentials are assigned inside `Prepare`, so a hook between `Claim` and `Prepare` follows no lease this attempt minted, and `ReclaimClaimed` (reclaim.go:76-80) only reaches leases another attempt or the original bind minted. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/binder.go:222-236; credentiallease.go:23-33
WATCHOUT: `ReleaseSlotReservation` (slotbinder.go:728) calls `SlotClaimer.ReleaseSlot` with recycle=false, so its occupancy-zero edge DELETEs the claim and never patches `recycling`; a sibling slot (ClaimSlot Pass 1 joining between the claim CREATE and the hook) keeps the claim. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podclaim/slotclaimer.go:858-899
OPEN: CODE-4 item 5.3 names only `failResume`, which is `Binder.Resume`-specific (it compensates the Resume's bindAttempt). On the snapshotless rebuild branch the `BindResult` comes from `Binder.Bind`/`BindSlot`, which minted leases and started a session; item 5.3 names no release for it, and the obvious `rollbackBinding`/`Binder.Release` revokes session-wide leases (release.go:66). Separate finding for a later round; not fixed here.

DECISION: `ReleaseSuspendedPod` runs off the serial Tick on a goroutine with its own per-replica in-flight set, pointing at the CODE-6 item 2.2 `ResumeBacklog` pattern, and its checkpoint context carries the §4.4 **Checkpoint timeout and recovery:** 60 s deadline, a deadline counting as a checkpoint failure that takes the existing 60 s retry — BECAUSE production wires `checkpointer.Checkpointer` with `Deadline` zero, so the checkpoint stream is unbounded on the gateway side, and `Watchdog.Run` calls `Tick` serially — ALTERNATIVES: sharing the backlog resume's in-flight set (rejected: a release's checkpoint, up to 60 s, would then defer a backlog resume, whereas run concurrently the resume wins through the row guards and step 3 releases nothing); one shared go-once helper across `DriveResume`, `ResumeBacklog`, and the release (more coherent, but it rewrites CODE-4 item 2 and item 2.2, so it is a refactor for a later round); setting `Checkpointer.Deadline` in `pod_lifecycle.go` (it also changes periodic checkpoints, which belongs to a separate finding).

### [non-spec.1.review-performance.1]
DECISION: Returned no findings in non-spec round 1 — BECAUSE the only changes since the r9 snapshot are checklist wording (S1-S5 labels, S? "Depends on: S1, S2"), the summary's restored open-decision list and deliverable-index wording, and one SPEC-5f sentence; none adds a store write, a watch, a per-row Redis call, or a store dependency. Traced the non-spec staging for top-tier cost and failure modes: StampSync per Send (one row UPDATE per batch; pgstore.Update always issues the UPDATE, pgstore.go:420-460) is smaller than the existing per-event AdvanceLastSeq row write; DriveResume's lease Get runs per resume_pending row (window-bounded population); ResumeBacklog/ResumeSuspended run off the Tick goroutine (CODE-6 item 2.2) — ALTERNATIVES: re-filing the sweepSuspended HeldLen probe (a Redis ZCOUNT per suspended row per replica per 5 s tick, run before the lease gate) against the 7-day population (refuted family, review-log WATCHOUT :670); an ambiguous Postgres COMMIT in completeResume, whose store-error branch CODE-4 item 5 leaves unstated beyond "when the guard fails" (not filed: rare, recoverable through the resuming watchdog and the orphan GC when the attempt simply stops; an implementor who releases on every Update error would leave a running row naming a released pod, so a later lens may want to check how the landed code handles it); mass-resume claim bursts after node loss (spec §7.3 already requires automatic retry, so not new to this proposal).
FACT: The watchdog Tick runs every sweep serially per tenant on every replica (pkg/gateway/runtime/watchdog/watchdog.go:588-680), and sweepMaxAge and the coordination Sweeper both list with an empty ListFilter, i.e. every row including terminal ones (watchdog.go:1075; coordination.go:303). Per-row listing cost over the suspended population is therefore pre-existing and not new to this proposal. EVIDENCE: as cited.
UNVERIFIED: completeResume's handling of a store error on the guarded commit Update that is not a guard miss (Postgres failover, lost COMMIT ack). CODE-4 item 5.3 states only the guard-miss branch. The implementor or the proposal-conformance pass should confirm the landed code does not release the pod on an ambiguous commit error without re-reading the row.
USEFUL [spec.1.review-performance.1 WATCHOUT, 7-day suspended population]: saved re-filing the HeldLen probe and lease scaling a sixth time.

### [non-spec.2.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: A lost commit releases its pod through a new `Binder.ReleaseUncommitted` (CODE-4 item 5.3): `ReleaseSlot` on a slot pool, `Release(result, "failed")` otherwise, with `releaseCredentials` factored out so it is skipped — BECAUSE every existing release that fits both branches revokes every lease of the session through `Credentials.ReleaseSession(sessionID)` — ALTERNATIVES: `failResume` (needs the Resume-local `bindAttempt` token no result carries, and uses the resume-reservation ledger that is wrong for the rebuild branch's Bind/BindSlot result); `rollbackBinding`/`Release`/`ReleaseSlot`/`ReclaimClaimed` (each calls `releaseCredentials`); a keep-credentials flag on `Release` (a dual mode).
WATCHOUT: Do not restore `failResume` or name `rollbackBinding` for the lost-commit release. `failResume` sends a reclaim keyed on `bindAttempt` (podsession/resume.go:151, :274), which the adapter answers SUPERSEDED for a foreign token (pkg/adapter/session.go:392-396, rule 13); `rollbackBinding` revokes the leases of a winning later attempt. EVIDENCE: sessionserver/bind_rollback.go:20-33; podsession/release.go:66; slotbinder.go:783; credentiallease.go:139-143.
FACT: `ReleaseSlot` calls `releaseCredentials` after the adapter Shutdown (slotbinder.go:775-783), while `Release` calls it first (release.go:66). The staged refactor moves it first in `ReleaseSlot` too; credential release and adapter teardown are independent, so the reorder is behaviour-neutral. EVIDENCE: podlifecycle/podsession/slotbinder.go:762-790.
DECISION: The rebuild branch publishes through `publishBinding`, and `resumeOnPod` no longer acquires the lease on its checkpoint branch (CODE-4 items 3.3, 4, 5.4); item 3.3's acquire is the one acquire — BECAUSE the tree forbids gating a post-commit publish on a second acquire (sessionserver/bind_registration.go:43-55), and the checkpoint-branch acquire's error path calls `rollbackBinding` (resume_rebind.go:117-118), which revokes session-wide leases — ALTERNATIVES: roll back the commit on a `registerBinding` error (the row would name a released pod); retry the acquire (unneeded).
CORRECTS [review-log.md:1474 "item 5.3 cites `failResume`"]: item 5.3 now names `ReleaseUncommitted`; the review-log OPEN at :1434/:1478 about `failResume`'s token is closed by it.

### [non-spec.2.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: The lost-commit release (CODE-4 item 5.3) is a new `Binder.ReleaseUncommitted(ctx, *BindResult)`: `Release(result, "failed")` on an exclusive pool and `ReleaseSlot` on a slot pool, without `releaseCredentials`, by factoring the credential release out of both — BECAUSE every existing post-RPC release revokes every lease of the session (`ReleaseSession`), which on a lost commit whose session continues (watchdog exit to `resume_pending`, then a re-entry at G+1) strips the leases the original bind or the winning attempt holds — ALTERNATIVES: `failResume` (needs the Resume's local `bindAttempt`, which no result carries, so the reclaim is answered SUPERSEDED; and `releaseResumeSlot` is the wrong ledger for the rebuild branch's Bind/BindSlot result); `rollbackBinding` (the finding's suggestion; Release and ReleaseSlot both call `releaseCredentials` → session-wide `ReleaseSession`, the defect [non-spec.1.fix-design-G1.1] already rejected it for); a `keepCredentials` flag on `Release` (a dual mode); returning `bindAttempt` on `BindResult` for a fenced teardown (new field on three constructors to fix a same-session-two-slots-one-pod case that every unconditional Release already has).
EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/release.go:60-66 (Release → releaseCredentials); slotbinder.go:762-788 (ReleaseSlot → unconditional Shutdown, releaseCredentials, SlotClaimer.ReleaseSlot); resume.go:151 (bindAttempt local), :176-200 (no attempt field); credassign.go:400-408 (ReleaseSession releases all leases of the session); sessionserver/finalize.go:505-522 (terminal finalize releases them anyway); bind_rollback.go:20-33.
FACT: Release and ReleaseSlot send the UNCONDITIONAL teardown form (adapterclient sets unconditional_teardown), which the adapter reclaims regardless of bind-attempt token (pkg/adapter/session.go:383-401, rule 12). Only the fenced form (failResume, compensateAndNote) needs the token. All three BindResult constructors set `Adapter` (bindlaunch.go:96, slotbinder.go:386, resume.go:176).

### [non-spec.2.fix-design-G3.1]
DECISION: A PostAgentOutput REJECT on a held message records the §16.7 audit row, transcribes and publishes nothing for that entry, removes it, and the loop continues; an audit-row write failure is a loop error (entry stays) — BECAUSE the REJECT is the gate's outcome, not a delivery failure (leaving the entry would block every later path-2 Send behind it), and the HTTP path fails closed with 500 on an audit failure — ALTERNATIVES: a new rejection event type on the event stream (rejected: no such event exists in the tree, new protocol surface for a case the audit row already records); treating REJECT as a Send error (rejected: wedges the queue head).
FACT: The PostAgentOutput chain, its audit row, and the HTTP error envelope are one call chain through the response writer: recordDeliveredResponse -> runPostAgentOutput(ctx, w, ...) -> recordRouteRejection(ctx, w, ...) -> writeError(w, ...) which calls w.Header() and panics on a nil writer. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/messages_delivery.go:309-330, route.go:117-126, route.go:169-186, error_envelope.go:36-39
WATCHOUT: Moving the envelope write out of runPostAgentOutput breaks TestRunPostAgentOutputRejectReturns403, which asserts the 403 through runPostAgentOutput's recorder. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/postagentoutput_internal_test.go:33-37

### [non-spec.3.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: `completeResume` (CODE-4 item 5) runs wholly on the server-lifetime context, and the attempt deadline (item 3.2, reset in item 3.4) bounds the attempt only up to the `completeResume` call — BECAUSE the deadline exists to bound how long a restore holds a pod, and a timer left armed past the commit cancels `deliverBuffered`'s `Send` mid-turn (PodExecutor.Send returns the ctx error and leaves the consumed turn to the reader, pkg/gateway/session/executor/pod.go:95-101), so the entry stays at the head and is re-sent with no crash or handoff, and it also cancels the fence, events, and `recoverDelegationTree` tail — ALTERNATIVES: timer.Stop() after the commit (an AfterFunc that already fired leaves the ctx cancelled); a ReleaseUncommitted exit on the step-1 lock wait (new exit clause, discards a restored pod); context.WithoutCancel per entry in deliverBuffered (closes only the double delivery); WithoutCancel(attemptCtx) for the tail (drops shutdown cancellation).
WATCHOUT: A post-deadline commit is safe only because step 2 is guarded on `resuming` and `G` and item 3.4 says correctness does not depend on the attempt ending before `sweepResuming`. Do not remove either when touching the deadline text. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-4 items 3.4 and 5.2.
OPEN: `resumeHeldAndDrain` (CODE-4 item 8) and the path-2 callers (CODE-6 item 7) run `deliverBuffered` on a request context, so a client disconnect mid-turn re-sends a held entry outside the RECORDS-1 7(i) duplicate allowance. Candidate remedy: send, record, and remove each entry on context.WithoutCancel(ctx) in CODE-4 item 6. Not landed here; it needs its own review.

### [non-spec.3.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: `completeResume` runs on the server-lifetime context, so the attempt deadline ends at the call (CODE-4 item 5 lead sentence; item 3.4 "holds its pod" -> "holds its pod before `completeResume`") — BECAUSE the deadline exists to bound a restore that holds a pod, and every post-commit step (publish, fence, events, recoverDelegationTree, deliverBuffered) must not be cut by it; the commit is guarded on G, so a commit after the deadline is safe (item 3.4 already says correctness does not depend on the attempt ending first) — ALTERNATIVES: stop the timer after the commit and keep the attempt context (rejected: AfterFunc can fire between the commit and Stop, and Stop=false leaves a cancelled context; needs a fresh context anyway); keep step 5.1 on the attempt context and add a lock-wait release exit (rejected: adds an exit that discards a restored pod for a brief lock wait; the server context leaves only the shutdown exit, which **Driver goroutine at shutdown** already states).
FACT: PodExecutor.Send cannot tell "cancelled before the envelope was written" from "cancelled mid-turn": both return the context error, and a mid-turn cancel leaves the turn to the reader, so the runtime consumed it — EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/session/executor/podstream.go runTurn/awaitReply; pkg/gateway/session/executor/pod.go Send doc comment. Any held-message Send on a cancellable context therefore risks double delivery on retry.
FACT: A turn with no caller deadline is still bounded by stream liveness: the adapter ends the stream with DEADLINE_EXCEEDED on a missed runtime heartbeat ack, and the end of the delivering request does not end the stream — EVIDENCE: spec/28_communication-channels.md CH-ATTACH **Timing.** and **Degradation.**
OPEN: Separate finding, not fixed in G1: deliverBuffered's other callers run it on a request context — `resumeHeldAndDrain` from `handleResume` (CODE-4 item 8) and the path-2 message paths (CODE-6 item 7, `SessionDelivery.DeliverHeld`). A client disconnect during a held-message turn cancels Send mid-turn, the entry stays at the head, and the next delivery point re-sends it: a duplicate with no crash or handoff, outside RECORDS-1 7(i). Candidate remedy in its one home, CODE-4 item 6: each entry's Send, record, and removal run on `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`, and the loop checks ctx only before taking the next entry. That remedy would also make G1's completeResume context change cover shutdown-mid-turn.
OPEN: CODE-4 item 5 step 3 specifies only a failed guard; a store error on the step-2 commit (outcome unknown) has no stated disposition. Not raised by G1; a later round may file it.

### [non-spec.3.fix-design-G3.1]
DECISION: The SPEC-5o budget-key TTL and re-arm get a carrier in CODE-6 (new item 14 plus the chart value in item 11): a `--delegation-budget-key-ttl-seconds` flag (default `treebudget.DefaultTTL`, raised to 691200 s) passed to `treebudget.New`, a startup refusal when it does not exceed `--max-suspended-session-seconds`, and a new `(*treebudget.Reserver).RearmTree` called after each committed write into or out of `suspended`. RECORDS-1 7(d) and the summary Defects bullet are replaced in place by the remaining pre-existing gap, the unbuilt §8.3 `BUDGET_KEYS_EXPIRED` sentinel — BECAUSE CODE-1 (active-time age) and CODE-6 (idle suspension, 604800 s suspended lifetime) make a root outlive the 24 h key TTL under defaults, which today the 7200 s wall-clock age cap prevents; the regression is this proposal's own, so recording it (round 2's answer) cannot close it — ALTERNATIVES: building the sentinel and the §8.3 cascade-cancel cleanup here (rejected: lazily created keys cannot tell a first reserve from an expired tree without a new tree-creation marker, plus a cascade path; a whole §8.3 feature, pre-existing, and unreachable under defaults once the TTL outlives each segment); a sliding TTL in the reserve script (rejected in an earlier round: changes the Lua contract and still expires an idle suspended tree); re-arming from the §11.2 checkpoint loop for every listed active tree (would keep keys alive for exactly the tree's life, but diverges from SPEC-5o, a spec-loop change); gating S13 on an external carrier (blocks the proposal on unfiled work).
FACT: Under defaults with the carrier, time between re-arms is bounded by one suspended period (≤ 604800 s) or one non-suspended period (active age ≤ 7200 s, since CODE-1 accrues only in starting/running/input_required, plus recovering windows of 900 s each), so the 691200 s TTL fires only for the SPEC-5 edge-case cycling root, a missed re-arm next to a long segment, or an operator `maxSessionAge` ≥ the TTL. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-1 item 2; spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:443.
WATCHOUT: `treebudget.DefaultTTL`'s doc comment says the TTL is "refreshed on every reserve"; the reserve script sets it only when `TTL == -1`. Do not rely on the comment. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/delegationtree/treebudget/treebudget.go:39-43, :179-181.
WATCHOUT: `RearmTree` keys on the session's own id for every row, root or not: a non-root has no `{id}:dlg:*` keys, so no root predicate is needed (`ParentSessionID` is overloaded by derive, sessionstore.go:143-151). It follows `PurgeRoot`'s SCAN of `{root}:dlg:*`. EVIDENCE: treebudget.go:474-500.
FACT: BUDGET_KEYS_EXPIRED appears in no Go code outside the alert description, and BUILD-GAPS.md has no finding for it; only TEST-GAPS.md (around :2615 and T-8.8.9) names it. EVIDENCE: pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:571.
CORRECTS [round-2 fix "Correct the TTL statement at its three sites"]: correcting the statement left the regression in place; the finding needed a code carrier, not a better record.

DECISION: `deliverBuffered` (CODE-4 item 6) runs each entry's `Send`, `recordDeliveredResponse`, and removal on the server-lifetime context and reads the caller's `ctx` only between entries — BECAUSE `PodExecutor.Send` returns the context error mid-turn after the runtime consumed the message, so a request-context caller (handleResume, path-2 REST, MCP DeliverHeld, ResumeSuspended) left a consumed entry at the head and the next delivery point re-sent it with a fresh envelope ID — ALTERNATIVES: `context.WithoutCancel` (escapes shutdown); moving each caller to the server-lifetime context (one rule at several sites); deriving the envelope ID from MessageID (no adapter dedup set exists). ### [non-spec.4.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: `deliverBuffered` runs each entry's `Send`, `recordDeliveredResponse`, and removal on the server-lifetime context (CODE-4 item 2), and reads its caller's `ctx` only before taking the next entry; the rule lives once in CODE-4 item 6 and covers every caller (completeResume, resumeHeldAndDrain from handleResume and ResumeSuspended, path-2 REST, MCP DeliverHeld, ResumeBacklog) — BECAUSE PodExecutor.Send returns the ctx error mid-turn while the runtime has consumed the message (pod.go Send doc comment; podstream.go awaitReply), and each envelope gets a fresh `newMessageID()`, so a request/tool-call cancel left a consumed entry at the head and the next delivery point re-sent it — ALTERNATIVES: `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (rejected: never cancelled at shutdown, so a handler blocks graceful shutdown until the stream ends, and it is a second context rule beside completeResume's); moving each caller onto the server-lifetime context (rejected: one rule stated at five sites); deriving the envelope ID from the held MessageID for adapter dedup (rejected: no `delivered_message_ids` set exists, RECORDS-1 7(i)).
DECISION: A shutdown that cancels the server-lifetime context mid-turn still leaves the consumed entry at the head; it is redelivered by the next coordinator, which is the crash/handoff duplicate RECORDS-1 7(i) already files. Not restated in staged text.
FACT: A turn on the server-lifetime context is still bounded: `awaitReply` returns on stream end (`c.done`), which the adapter heartbeat escalation and 0091's CH-ATTACH stream-failure rule produce for a hung runtime. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/session/executor/podstream.go awaitReply.
WATCHOUT: Test the context rule once, at `deliverBuffered` (TestDeliverBufferedCallerCancelMidTurnDeliversOnce); do not add per-caller variants through handleResume and DeliverHeld, because no caller chooses the context any more.
WATCHOUT: Tier-8 held-pod `suspended` kill: a message sent to the holder would resume synchronously and never be held across the kill. Send it through the surviving replica after the kill and before the lease lapses (non-holder answers `queued`, writes nothing), so it is in the DLQ when the peer adopts. Assert at-least-once (RECORDS-1 7(i)) plus an empty DLQ.
DECISION: This closes the review-log OPEN "A client disconnect during a held-message turn cancels Send mid-turn ..." (review-log ledger near :1797, :1827).

### [non-spec.6.review-reliability.1]
DECISION: Returned no findings under the reliability lens for non-spec round 6. BECAUSE the round-5 diff (the CODE-6 item 2.1 `errSuspendedSuperseded` miss handling, the expiry test that asserts the terminal-hook calls, and `TestSendMessageBufferedRunsPreMessageDelivery` widened to the `input_required` inbox branch) changes no recovery mechanism. I re-traced every held-message edge on and off the coordinating replica and found no new loss, double-apply, leak, or stall. The edges were: idle suspension with the backlog check ahead of the zero-hold release; the release racing a held-pod resume through the `holdsPod` guard and `errResumeHeldPodReleased`; the podless and held-pod resume; admission refusal and re-route after the suspend write; the commit followed by `deliverBuffered`; a coordinator crash after the `running` commit; a serving-replica crash between the DLQ enqueue and the state write; and an enqueue racing a terminal write. ALTERNATIVES: (1) The expiry sweep's stale `resuming` listing double outcome. Rejected because it was already weighed twice (review-log.md:1603, :2048). (2) Clock skew in the interrupt backlog predicate. Rejected because it was already weighed (review-log.md:975, :1372). (3) The `ReleaseSuspendedPod` step-3 guard carries no `coordination_generation`, so a replica that lost its lease mid-checkpoint can still clear `PodAssignment` after a peer re-adopted the pod. Rejected as below the bar: it needs the lease to be lost while the replica is still alive and a peer to adopt within the 60 s checkpoint. If it happens, the session recovers through the orphan-claim GC and the stream-failure edge.
FACT: `sweepDLQExpiry` lists rows by state and calls `SweepExpired` with no state re-check, and `SweepExpired` is an atomic Lua take. Any race between expiry and delivery therefore comes from the stale listing alone. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/runtime/watchdog/watchdog.go:684-705; pkg/gateway/session/sessioninbox/dlq.go:156-163
FACT: The 0091 Sweeper keeps the lease of a session with no binding through the `priorHolder == s.replicaID` renew. A podless `suspended` or `resume_pending` session therefore keeps its coordinator, which is what the CODE-4 item 14 lease-gate dependency and the backlog-resume gate rely on. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/coordination/coordination/coordination.go:375, :427
USEFUL [review-log:2048]: it saved re-deriving the expiry-versus-delivery race.

### [non-spec.11.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: CODE-4 item 5.3 is the one home of the commit-miss classification; item 5.2 only retries on a store error. A miss counts as landed only when it follows a store error and the row the guard read is in neither a terminal nor a recovery state and names the attempt's sandbox; at `G` run step 4 (steps 5 and 6 only when `running`), above `G` publish and release nothing (CODE-5 item 2 readopt owns the pod); every other miss calls `ReleaseUncommitted` — BECAUSE the round-10 success conjunction (running ∧ sandbox ∧ G ∧ RG+1) released a pod a live row named after a row-only interrupt `suspended` write or a takeover `RecordHandoff` — ALTERNATIVES: reviewer's `G` ∧ RG+1 witness (fails under takeover, needs the item 3.1 baseline the binderless path lacks); RG-above-baseline witness on the binder path (attempt B's commit raises RG too, so A leaks); guarding the interrupt fallback (closes path (a) only).
WATCHOUT: The design as supplied classified EVERY miss by the sandbox witness. On a concurrent pool `PodAssignment` is the shared pod name (pod_claim.go ClaimResult doc: SandboxName persisted on row.PodAssignment), so attempt A's clean miss against attempt B's commit on another slot of the same pod would read "landed above G" and leak A's slot and leases; and a recovery-state row keeps the failed pod's name (failure.go stamps rep.PodAssignment; pod_launch.go:183-192), so a watchdog-exited row at `G` could read "landed at G" and publish a binding on `resume_pending`. Hence the two added conditions (after a store error; not a recovery state). Do not drop either. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/pod_claim.go:85-90; failure.go:337-338
FACT: At `G`, the only non-recovery, non-terminal successor of the `resuming` row is A's own commit: interrupt admits no `resuming` row, failure reporters need a published binding (none before step 4), and `sweepResuming` exits to `resume_pending` without a bump. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/interrupt.go:55-58 (EndpointInterrupt precondition); session_transitions.go:119
OPEN: Residual after a lost ack on a concurrent pool: landed, adopted at G+1, then failed to `resume_pending` naming the sandbox, item 5.3 calls `ReleaseUncommitted` on a pod the next attempt's `releaseEarlierBinding` also releases (possible double `ReleaseSlot`); and a lost-ack miss against attempt B's commit on the same pod reads as landed-above-G and leaks A's slot. Both need ack loss plus a watchdog exit or takeover inside one commit retry loop. A reliability lens should decide whether a per-attempt witness (none exists on the row today) is warranted.
OPEN: A landed commit whose row is already `suspended` skips the item 5.5 tail (no `session.resumed` audit, no status change), per the design; an audit-completeness lens should confirm that is acceptable.
DECISION: Binderless clause (CODE-4 item 2) substitutes `RecoveryGeneration` above the row `DriveResume` received for the sandbox and `G`, and takes the `G` branch — BECAUSE after CODE-4 item 4 deletes `bumpRecoveryGeneration` only a `completeResume` commit raises it, and binderless rows have no `PodAssignment`, so CODE-5 never readopts them.

### [non-spec.11.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: A `completeResume` guard miss is classified by whether the row the guard read names the attempt's sandbox (CODE-4 item 5.3), on every miss rather than only on a repeat: names it at `G` and non-terminal → publish (step 4), tail and delivery only when `running`; names it above `G` and non-terminal → a peer's readopt owns the pod, do nothing; otherwise (terminal, or names no/another pod) → `ReleaseUncommitted` — BECAUSE the replacement sandbox is written into `PodAssignment` only by this attempt's commit, so naming it is a state-independent witness that the commit landed, and the release decision then follows CODE-6 item 4's invariant directly — ALTERNATIVES: the round-10 conjunctive repeat-success predicate (`running` ∧ sandbox ∧ `G` ∧ `RecoveryGeneration` = base+1), which released the pod on any later state change (interrupt row-only `suspended`, takeover to G+1); a `RecoveryGeneration`-above-base witness on the binder path (wrong: attempt A at G, watchdog exit, attempt B commits at G+1 → A would see RG above base and leak its pod).
WATCHOUT: `handleInterrupt`'s row-only fallback writes `suspended` with no state guard in its mutator and keeps `PodAssignment`, and it takes no delivery lock, so it can land between a lost-ack commit and the repeat. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/interrupt.go:63-66, :84-89; session_transitions.go `transitionInterrupt`.
FACT: The only `RecoveryGeneration` increment in the tree is `bumpRecoveryGeneration` (session_generation.go:74), which CODE-4 item 4 deletes; after 0092 only `completeResume`'s step 2 bumps it. This is what makes the binderless witness (RG above the row `DriveResume` received) sound. EVIDENCE: grep `RecoveryGeneration++` pkg cmd.
OPEN: A landed commit whose row is no longer `running` at the miss (interrupt or idle suspension before the repeat) runs no item 5.5 tail, so no `session.resumed` audit row or resumed event is written for a resume that did occur. Chosen because the tail announces a `running` session after a later status change already reached the client; an audit-completeness lens may want only the counter and audit row to run.

### [non-spec.11.fix-design-G2.1]
DECISION: A `HeldLen` error skips the row for that tick (no `ResumeBacklog`, no release) and is not returned from `sweepSuspended`, stated as one sentence appended to CODE-6 item 2.2 that points at `sweepDLQExpiry` — BECAUSE propagating aborts the serial per-tenant `Tick` (later sweeps and later tenants), and treating the error as zero lets sub-item 3 release an `Idle` row's pod with an unread backlog — ALTERNATIVES: propagate as `Tick` does for store errors (rejected: stalls every sweep during a Redis reset); treat as zero (rejected: releases a pod whose backlog is unknown); a sweep-wide "every per-row error skips the row" rule at item 2 (rejected here: also re-scopes item 2.1's store Update error, which no finding examined; see OPEN).

### [non-spec.12.review-performance.1]
FACT: On a concurrent pool the slot ID is the session ID ("SlotID equals SessionID"; "one session occupies exactly one slot"), and `PodAssignment` holds `SandboxName`, the shared pod name. A second slot of the same session on the same pod would share the first slot's key. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/slotbinder.go:150; pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podclaim/slotclaimer.go:211, :774; pkg/gateway/sessionserver/create.go:356
UNVERIFIED: CODE-4 item 5.3 says a guard miss "above G" means a takeover, so it publishes nothing and releases nothing. Suppose a replica loses its Postgres connection for longer than MaxResumingSeconds while its lease lapses (the Sweeper's List fails, so it does not renew; coordination.go:303-305). A peer can then exit A's incarnation, adopt the session, and commit B on the same concurrent pod, and A's repeat misreads B's commit as its own. Whether B can reserve a slot on A's pod while A's same-key slot is live, and so whether A's slot and its minted leases leak, depends on SlotClaimer's handling of a duplicate session ID. Nobody has checked this. The concurrent-pool lost-commit test ("both slots on one pod", non-spec-changes Tier 1 driver bullet) assumes the duplicate is possible, and the implementor should confirm that against slotclaimer.go.
FACT: A coordination lease read that fails already failed closed before this proposal (acquireCoordinationLease aborts on a Redis error, coordination_lease.go:34-45). The Design lease gate's refusal during a Redis outage is therefore no worse than the shipped behaviour.

No row reaches `running`/`input_required` from the unpublished binding except through the commit itself, because the executor has no binding until step 4. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md:76-78.

### [mechanism.podless-session-coordination.1]

CORRECTS [Standing context Settled "Lease retention."]: it stated renewal in every non-terminal state except `created`, `finalizing`, and `ready`, and cited the §29.3 terminate row as the reason. A podless `suspended` session holds no lease (SPEC-2a), and SPEC-2d corrects the terminate row, which listed `suspended` as a lease-holding state.

FACT: The shipped `eligible` renews any lease held by this replica, bound or not, so the exclusion must come before `eligible` and override `bound` as well as `priorHolder`. It comes before the dead-connection branch too, which would otherwise release the lease of a bound podless row and leave its mirror row unreleased. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/coordination/coordination/coordination.go:355, :375.
FACT: `coordlease.Store.Upsert` clears `released_at`, so a one-shot mirror release at the suspension release is undone by a sweep that listed the row before the clear and renews after it. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/coordination/coordlease/coordlease.go:114.
FACT: `enterResumePending` is guarded on `!holdsPod` of the locked row (CODE-4 item 9), and the release's step 3 is a guarded `Update`. Both run on the primary, so a hold followed by the guarded write and a clear followed by one backlog check leave no podless row with an unnoticed held message outside the residual SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.** states. A gateway with no pod binder reports every row as holding a pod, so `sweepSuspended` skips a row only when `holdsPod` is false, and a binderless row keeps the backlog evaluation. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-4 item 9, CODE-6 item 4 step 3; pgstore.Get reads the replica (pkg/gateway/session/sessionstore/pgstore/pgstore.go:354-357).
FACT: The freshness reaper counts `suspended` as active with no pod check. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/checkpoint/checkpointer/freshness.go:206-215.
DECISION: `awaiting_client_action` keeps 0091's retention. BECAUSE: the state is bounded at 900 s (spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:443), the holder's driver restores with no lapse or handoff after a resume call, and 0091's Invariant records that §29.6 **Preconditions.** and the §7.2 durable-inbox rows assume a coordinator there. ALTERNATIVES: drop the lease on entry, which reverses 0091 and adds a 60 s lapse and a handoff before every restore.
DECISION: The terminal write from podless `suspended` takes no new guard. BECAUSE: from podless `suspended` the row reaches only `resume_pending`, `expired`, or a terminal state, and a terminal write that lands in `resume_pending` or `resuming` is settled by the driver's generation compare-and-swap (spec-changes.md edge case "Terminate or cancel racing the driver").
DECISION: The Sweeper releases the mirror row of a podless `suspended` session while it is still the prior holder, and keeps its lease read for such rows. BECAUSE: the release repeats until the lease lapses, so a concurrent re-upsert cannot leave the row live, and it needs no new `Server` option. ALTERNATIVES: skip podless rows before the lease read and release the mirror once in the suspension release, which saves one Redis GET per podless row per replica per sweep and leaves the re-upsert race open (OD-P1).
DECISION: No periodic backlog evaluation of a podless `suspended` session, and no indexes on the `suspended` listings. BECAUSE: the guarded write after each hold and the one check at the release cover every message outside the residual SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.** states, and the podless rows then cost no `HeldLen` call. ALTERNATIVES: keep the per-replica evaluation, run it on the gateway leader, or add migration 0183 with two partial indexes (OD-P2, OD-P3).
DECISION: The 300 s `resuming` watchdog stays, and the rebuild bound is filed as RECORDS-1 item 7(m). BECAUSE: the orphan-claim GC reclaims the unreferenced replacement claim after `claimOrphanTimeout`, so raising the watchdog alone does not let a long rebuild finish.
DECISION: A restore with no credential provider assigns no lease (SPEC-1g). The fail-open on a failed tenant or runtime lookup predates 0092 and is filed as RECORDS-1 item 7(n). EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/credential_preclaim.go:110-136.
WATCHOUT: Do not reintroduce a forward or an adoption for any podless `suspended` §29.3 row. Interrupt and upload do not admit `suspended`, and resume and messages are store writes under SPEC-3j and SPEC-5l.
WATCHOUT: Do not restore a periodic `HeldLen` probe on podless rows without first showing a message that the guarded write after the hold and the check at the release both miss, outside the residual SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.** states.

### [redesign2.apply.1]

DECISION: The podless-session coordination redesign (2026-10-09) was applied from `scratchpad/redesign/0092_new_write-the-session-suspend-and-resume-proposal-that-gateway-redesign-1.md`. Every edit it lists applied, 1 to 42 with the lettered additions; each anchor resolved exactly once, and no edit was skipped. It redesigned three areas: lease holding for a podless `suspended` session (SPEC-2a, new SPEC-2d, CODE-5 item 1), the custody of held messages for such a session (SPEC-5i **Held messages.** and **Backlog resume.**, CODE-6 items 2, 4 step 3a, 7, and 12), and the checkpoint freshness gauge (SPEC-5c, CODE-6 item 15). The reason was that on-demand adoption had no caller, the events JSON form needed no holder, and every replica probed every podless row's backlog every 5 s for the whole suspended lifetime.
DECISION: Deleted by the redesign: on-demand adoption in SPEC-2a; RECORDS-1 item 7(l) as written (the missing on-demand adoption) and its summary **Defects** bullet; the events JSON row's forward in §29.3 and "events JSON" in the forwarding-row list; the periodic backlog evaluation of a podless row; the `HeldLen` call `sweepSuspended` made before any lease check; "writes nothing" for an off-holder hold to a held-pod row; and the lease renewal of a bound podless row. RECORDS-1 item 7 now carries (l) unindexed listings, (m) the rebuild bound, (n) the credential lookup fail-open, and (o) the §10.4 replay buffer.
DECISION: Reconciliation beyond the redesign's own edits: the CODE-5 item 3 comments name the podless exclusion; the summary gains three watch-outs (the skip placement before `eligible` and the dead-connection branch, the primary-side ordering of the hold write and the release check, and the `HoldsPod` binderless case); checklist S2 names the §29.3 rows and S6 depends on S2 as well as S5; the Standing context **Custody home.** entry names the guarded write after a podless hold.
OPEN: OD-P1 (mirror release in the Sweeper, default, or once in the suspension release), OD-P2 (no indexes on the `suspended` listings, default, or migration 0183), OD-P3 (no periodic backlog evaluation of podless rows, default, or per-replica or leader evaluation), and OD-P4 (file the §10.4 and §15.1 replay-buffer inconsistency as RECORDS-1 item 7(o), default, or rewrite the §15.1 cell in SPEC-2d). The staged text applies each default; the summary's open-decisions section lists them.
WATCHOUT: Replaced: on-demand adoption of a podless `suspended` session before a §29.3 row that needs a coordinator. No inter-replica forward exists to call it, terminate, delete, and resolution already run on any replica with no lease check, and the events JSON form reads relay history on any replica. Do not re-add an adoption or a forward for a podless row; SPEC-2d states the rows.
WATCHOUT: Replaced: the periodic backlog evaluation of every podless `suspended` row on every replica every 5 s. It cost one `HeldLen` per row per replica per tick over the 7-day population. The guarded `enterResumePending` after each hold and the one backlog check at the release cover every message outside the residual SPEC-5i **Backlog resume.** states (OD-P3).
WATCHOUT: Replaced: lease renewal of a bound podless row and the one-shot mirror release in the suspension release (Specification 2, step 5 with `Options.CoordinationMirror`). `coordlease.Store.Upsert` clears `released_at`, so a sweep that listed the row before the clear re-upserts the mirror after a one-shot release. The Sweeper releases the mirror on every sweep while it is the prior holder (OD-P1).
WATCHOUT: Replaced: migration 0183 with `ListFilter.SuspendedAtOrBefore` and `ListFilter.SuspendedPodHeld`. The Sweeper, the freshness reaper, and the other watchdog sweeps still list unindexed, and podless rows no longer need backlog Redis work. RECORDS-1 item 7(l) files the listings (OD-P2).

DECISION: Deleted by the redesign: the `podsession.ErrOnClaimed` sentinel and its test; `isTransientPodClaimError`, `errResumeHoldStale`, and their tests; the `coordinatingReplica` refusal details key; the chart value `gateway.maxClientIdleSeconds`; the `failResume` doc paragraph "It releases no §4.9 credential lease."; the session-wide release on the `Bind` reconnect and launch failures; the summary's open-decision list; and every entry of the Open section.
DECISION: Reconciliation beyond the redesign's own edits: the DOCS-1a Content paragraph drops the retry-accounting sentence, which N25 moved to DOCS-1b; the lease-preserving release moved from Decision 8 to Non-goals; Decision 22 drops its comparison with the backlog resume; Decision 2 says the driver adds no state edge; the summary gains two watch-outs (the `slotAccountLocks` ordering of the suspension and funnel releases, and the attempt-scoped `Bind` release); the checklist S1 and S3 lines and the CODE-3 deliverable-index line name the new content. WATCHOUT: Replaced: the session-wide `ReleaseSession` on the `Bind` reconnect and launch failures. It revokes a lease another attempt minted for the same session. The `attemptScoped` request releases the attempt's own `PrepareResult.MintedLeaseIDs`; the decomposed `/finalize` and `/start` path keeps the session-wide release.
WATCHOUT: Replaced: the unlocked suspension release (CODE-6 item 4 step 4) and the funnel's release after `unlock()`. Each let a same-replica resume assign leases that the later `releaseCredentials` revoked. Both now hold `slotAccountLocks` across `releaseExecutor`; do not narrow the funnel lock back to slot bindings.
WATCHOUT: Replaced: the `coordinatingReplica` refusal details key and the chart value `gateway.maxClientIdleSeconds`. Neither has a spec basis. Do not re-add either.
