### [non-spec.6.review-performance.1]
DECISION: returned no findings in non-spec round 6. BECAUSE the r5-to-r6 delta has three parts: the CODE-6 item 7 read-pool fallback on a non-`ErrNotFound` `ReadPrimary` error, the `DeliverHeld` read-error-returns-nil clause, and two test additions (the `BindingGeneration` production test and the failing-`Update` case of `TestMessagePathsClassifyPrimaryRow`). None of them adds a store write, a watch, or a store dependency. Under a §12.3 failover the MCP path-2 trace is: fallback row `running`, then a `DeliverHeld` read failure (WARN, nil), then the `StampSync` fail-open, so it delivers as shipped. A stale held row on the fallback goes through `holdMessage`, whose failed re-read answers `inbox_unavailable`, which fails closed and loses nothing. ALTERNATIVES: (1) filing per-message primary cost (two `ReadPrimary` row-lock transactions plus the uncoalesced `StampSync` `UPDATE` per MCP path-2 send, against the §12.3 Tier 3 budget of ~300/s session-state writes and ~1,300/s total). Rejected: OD-A (owner) settled the per-Send write and redesign 6 settled the primary read. (2) Filing hang-versus-fail latency of the primary calls under a blackholed primary (pgconn's default dialer has no connect timeout). Rejected: `StampSync` has the same exposure and it was accepted under OD-A. (3) Filing the delegate_task `DeliverHeld` read failure that leaves a running child's held entries until the next delivery point. Rejected: this is the same class as the accepted **Held read failure.** outcome.
FACT: CODE-4 item 23.2's `LeaseStore.Lookup` returns a scan, KMS, or decode error as an error rather than as not-found, so a Postgres failover makes renewal retry rather than drop leases through `ErrLeaseReleased`. The Traps line "scanLease folds errors into not-found" describes the old scan path. It does not describe `Lookup`. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-4 item 23.2
FACT: shipped `Stamper.Stamp` coalesces to at most one async write per second per session with a 5 s persist timeout, while `StampSync` "never skips the write for coalescing". The per-Send primary write rate is therefore new with OD-A. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/session/sessionidle/sessionidle.go:139,174-184,228; non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 5.1
USEFUL [non-spec.5.review-performance.1]: its REST `requireTenantNotSuspended` WATCHOUT saved re-deriving the REST failover baseline.

### [non-spec-recheck.1.fix-design-G2.1]
DECISION: `DeliverHeld` on a `ReadPrimary` error other than `ErrNotFound` falls back to the `s.store.Get` (read-pool) row and delivers when that row is `running`; an error of that fallback read is returned, so the MCP path handles it as an error of the new message's `executor.Send` (§7.2 **Delivery of held messages.**: the path-2 message is handled as if its own delivery failed). BECAUSE `deliverBuffered(ctx, row)` needs a real row (`recordDeliveredResponse` uses `row.ID`, `row.TenantID`, and `recordTTFTOnce(row, ...)`), and this mirrors the CODE-6 item 7 classification fallback that already lets a `running` target keep path-2 delivery through a §12.3 failover. ALTERNATIVES: (a) the reviewer's literal fix, call `deliverBuffered` on the error (rejected: no row to pass, and its justification "Send to a non-running row fails in streamFor or the admitter" is false during a failover, where the item 5.5 admitter fails open per SPEC-5f); (b) change `DeliverHeld` to take the caller's classified row (rejected: `delegate_task` has only the `session.State` that `MaterializeDelegatedChild` returns, and it cascades into rule 1 and `TestDeliverHeldReadsPrimary_spec_7_2`); (c) return the `ReadPrimary` error at once (rejected: fails every MCP path-2 message through a primary failover, undoing the settled classification fallback); (d) return nil on the fallback read's failure too (rejected: the new message then overtakes unread-but-held entries, which the spec's exemption covers only for an inbox or DLQ read failure).
FACT: `recordDeliveredResponse` reads row fields beyond IDs (`recordTTFTOnce(row, "response")`). EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/messages_delivery.go:309-368.
CORRECTS [review-log DECISION at review-log.md:420 "`DeliverHeld` treats its own `ReadPrimary` error as a held read failure (WARN, nil)"]: a row read failure is not an inbox or DLQ read failure under §7.2 **Delivery of held messages.**; returning nil lets the MCP path-2 message overtake readable DLQ entries. The fallback-then-return-error rule above replaces it.
WATCHOUT: the rule-1 parenthesis in Design **Session-row read authority.** ("the first of which falls back to the read-pool row") counts which reads fall back; it must change with any fallback added or removed. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md:17.

FOR UPDATE` then rollback, which takes a row lock (WAL heap-lock record, xid) per call; REST path 2 pays 1 plus `StampSync`, MCP pays 2 plus `StampSync`. Spec gives no message rate, only gateway→pod RPC ~2,000/s at Tier 3 (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:263) against a ~1,600 IOPS sustained primary ceiling (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:115-121). Not filed: `StampSync` per Send is owner-settled (summary Decision 16, OD-A) and is the same order, and non-spec.6 rejected the read cost as settled by redesign 6; a plain primary-pool SELECT would cut the lock cost without changing the rule if a later owner review wants it. (2) Redis outage holding idle-suspended pods (`HeldLen` error returns true, no release): no worse than shipped, which held the idle pod to the 7200 s idle bound.
FACT: the watchdog already issues one `List` per state per tenant per tick (5 s, `DefaultTickInterval`) and `sweepMaxAge` lists every row, so `sweepSuspended`'s listing adds one indexed state query per tenant per tick and podless rows were already listed every tick — EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/runtime/watchdog/watchdog.go:166, :588-604, :1074-1075
FACT: §16 documents a Tier 4 (100,000 sessions, 2,000/s creation, 5,000 tenants) above Tier 3; the leader re-check at Tier 4 is ~100,000 `HeldLen` calls plus 5,000 tenant listings per 300 s pass (~350 Redis ops/s), within one pass interval at ~1 ms per call — EVIDENCE: spec/16_observability.md:595-598
USEFUL [non-spec.6.review-performance.1]: its rejected-alternatives list (per-message primary cost, blackholed-primary hang) saved re-deriving both and placed them under OD-A and redesign 6.
USEFUL [Settled: Leader capacity.]: bound held at Tier 3; extended above to Tier 4.

### [non-spec-recheck.1.review-reliability.1]
FACT: the REST path-2 `deliverBuffered` call reads no session row (it peeks the inbox and DLQ only), while the MCP path-2 call goes through `SessionDelivery.DeliverHeld`, which does its own `ReadPrimary` first. Under a Postgres primary error the two paths therefore diverge. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-4 item 6 (Loop bullet), CODE-6 item 7 `SessionDelivery` bullet.
WATCHOUT: the new "a `ReadPrimary` error is logged at WARN and returns nil" in `DeliverHeld` makes the MCP path-2 message overtake readable held DLQ entries during a primary failover. SPEC-5i **Delivery of held messages.** exempts only an inbox or DLQ read failure from the held-before-path-2 order. Filed as a finding; the remedy is to call `deliverBuffered` on a read error rather than return nil (a non-running row then fails in `streamFor` or the admitter and leaves the entry at the head). EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md:217, spec-changes.md:531.
FACT: `gatewayleader.Gate.Run` re-invokes every job's `Run` on each `OnStartedLeading`, so CODE-6 item 16.3's "`Run` calls `Pass` once when it starts" does give evaluation at once on every Lease acquisition. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/coordination/gatewayleader/gatewayleader.go:222-229, :142-147.
FACT: `Binder.Release` releases credentials before the teardown (release.go:66), so a step-4 teardown error after `releasePodCredentials` does not leave the pre-suspension leases renewing.

### [non-spec-recheck.3.review-reliability.1]
DECISION: no reliability findings in non-spec-recheck round 3. BECAUSE the diff against non-spec-recheck-r1-prefix is the same four hunks that round 2 reviewed: rule 1 names the `bufferAfterResumedSendFailure` re-read, rule 2 adds `sweepIdle` through `SuspendIdle`, `DeliverHeld` falls back to `s.store.Get`, and the failing-`Update` and fresh-state tests were extended. No staging changed after round 2. A whole-document walk of CODE-4 items 1-24, CODE-5, CODE-6 items 2, 4, 5, 7, and 16, and the Design paragraphs found no non-idempotent replay, unreclaimed resource, or unbounded wait that earlier rounds had not already settled. ALTERNATIVES: filing the adopter `TurnInFlight` gap (see the OPEN below). I rejected it because it is narrow and it improves on shipped behaviour, which expires the session terminally on any replica. Its remedy is also an owner trade-off between holding the pods of adopted idle sessions and suspending a silent turn, and neither choice is a required fix.
CORRECTS [Standing context Open, "UNVERIFIED: whether an adopter's `TurnInFlight` can idle-suspend a turn the dead coordinator started"]: verified. It can, but only for a turn that produces no other qualifying activity. On the sidecar transport, `Attach` returns on `ctx.Done` and does not signal the runtime, so the turn keeps running after the coordinator dies. EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/attach.go:186-187, and the heartbeat comment at attach.go:70-73. In the tree, the only stamps outside the proxy, direct-mode, and await_children paths are the `response`/`response_degraded` publishes. They happen after `Send` returns on the replica that sent the turn. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/events.go:362-369, messages_delivery.go:361,376. Proxy-mode chunks are stamped on whichever replica serves the proxy. EVIDENCE: cmd/lenny-gateway/llmproxy_usage.go:250-253. A turn that keeps calling the LLM is therefore protected after a handoff. A turn running a long tool with no LLM traffic for `maxClientIdleSeconds` after its admission stamp is not protected: the adopter's `SuspendIdle` sees no cached conn, suspends the session, and the zero hold releases the pod mid-turn.
OPEN (owner): summary.md:47 says the lease gate makes `SuspendIdle` correct. That stops holding after a handoff, because the new lease holder does not hold the turn. One possible remedy is a `TurnInFlight` that reports "unknown" (true) when this replica has no cached conn for an adopted `running` session. Its cost is that every idle session adopted after a rolling update keeps its pod until its next message or until the active-age cap. That trade-off is the owner's to make.
USEFUL [non-spec-recheck.2.review-reliability.1]: its trace of `recordDeliveredResponse` writing no session row settled the failing-`Update` test case without re-deriving it.

### [spec.6.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: close the release-time turn window by having `ReleaseSuspendedPod` hold the per-session delivery lock from after its checkpoint (before step 2a) until step 4 returns, and by adding one clause to SPEC-5f ("hands the session's runtime no message from that answer until the pod is released") — BECAUSE only the coordinating replica hands messages to the runtime and every such hand-off on that replica (both message paths, `deliverBuffered`, `completeResume`, `resumeHeldAndDrain`, `handleStart`) already runs under that lock, so holding it closes the gap with no new protocol surface — ALTERNATIVES: an adapter "refuse later message frames" mode on the pre-release `AttachTurnState` (new protocol surface and a resume-time un-refuse); making admission fail closed (reverses the settled OD-A/§12.3 fail-open); accepting the window (barred by the redesign-8 directive).
WATCHOUT: holding the lock only until the step-3 clear (what the reviewer suggested) leaves the window open. After the clear, a coordinator message path whose `ReadPrimary` fails falls back to the stale `running` entry row (I2), its `StampSync` fails during the failover, and `Send` reaches the still-bound executor stream before step 4 releases the binding. The lock must span step 2a through step 4. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md Design **Message-path read failures.** I2; CODE-6 item 5.5; CODE-6 item 4 step 4.
FACT: holding the delivery lock while waiting on `slotAccountLocks` in step 4 is deadlock-free only while nothing takes the delivery lock while it holds `slotAccountLocks`. Today `slotAccountLocks` is taken only in `applyFailureFromActive` (pkg/gateway/sessionserver/failure.go:207) and `releaseEarlierBinding` (resume_rebind.go:169), and neither takes a delivery lock under it. `PodExecutor.Release` does not wait on `c.done` (archive FACT, pod.go:257-270). EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/failure.go:199-230, resume_rebind.go:168-178.
CORRECTS [review-log Traps **Replaced: migrate before the clear.**]: the release now holds the delivery lock (from step 2a through step 4), so "the release takes no delivery lock" is false. Clear-first stays as the order.
DECISION: close the migration-versus-terminal-drain race in the migration's own home (SPEC-5z item 11). After a migration at a pod release, the gateway re-reads the session (`ReadPrimary`), runs the §7.3 terminal DLQ drain (`drainMessagingOnTerminal`) when the row is terminal, and leaves the entries in the DLQ when the re-read fails — BECAUSE the SPEC-5i **Enqueue racing a terminal transition.** rule answers a requester and removes entries when the re-read fails. Migrated entries were already answered, so extending that rule to the migration would make a store blip delete acknowledged messages and leave the implementor nothing to "answer" — ALTERNATIVES: the reviewer's one-clause SPEC-5i scope extension (misapplied answer and removal clauses); migrating before the clear under the new lock and draining when the clear's guard misses on a terminal row (reverses the settled clear-first order for no gain over the re-read).
CORRECTS [review-log Traps **Accepted migration windows.**]: a terminal drain racing the release migration is now reclaimed by SPEC-5z item 11's re-read. Only a crash, and a failed re-read on a session that is already terminal, leave entries without a reclaimer.

### [spec.6.follow-up-fix.1]
DECISION: non-spec CODE-6 item 4 step 4 now says the binding is either released before the attempt claims or removed by `releaseEarlierBinding` and skipped; the "or the attempt replaced" branch and the `SandboxName`-reuse rationale are deleted and replaced by one sentence: the delivery lock held from step 2a keeps the attempt's `completeResume` (CODE-4 item 5.1) from publishing before step 4 returns — BECAUSE `completeResume` takes the delivery lock at item 5.1 before its `running` write and publishes at 5.4, so on the releasing replica no replacement can be in the registry during step 4 — ALTERNATIVES: keeping the pointer-identity rationale (describes an unreachable interleaving; `releaseReportedBinding` still compares by pointer, so nothing is lost).
DECISION: TEST-1 Tier 7a `TestSuspensionReleaseRacingResumeKeepsNewLeases` slot-pool case rewritten: hold step 4 before it takes `slotAccountLocks` until the attempt's `completeResume` waits on the delivery lock, assert no binding is published while held, then let step 4 run and assert the replacement binding, slot, and leases survive and no `session.pod_released_during_suspension` is emitted. It now discriminates holding the delivery lock through step 4 — BECAUSE the old case ("hold step 4 until completeResume has published") deadlocks against the step-2a lock. Holding before `slotAccountLocks` is load-bearing: holding after it would block the attempt's `releaseEarlierBinding` and the attempt would never reach `completeResume`.
DECISION: Design **Session-row read authority.** rule (1) site list gains "the post-migration re-read of `ReleaseSuspendedPod` step 3 (CODE-6 item 4)".

### [spec.6.review-performance.1]
DECISION: no performance or failure-mode finding in the staged spec edits for round 6. BECAUSE the redesign-8 turn check adds one unary `AttachTurnState` RPC per idle-clock firing on the coordinator and one per `Idle` release attempt, with no Postgres, Redis, or etcd write. The admission write now carries only the activity stamp, so it adds fewer writes than the redesign-7 row boundary. Every new value that bounds the design is durable (Postgres row, shared lease record) or lives in the adapter (the turn count, which survives a coordinator handoff). ALTERNATIVES: filing the failover window at the `Idle` release (rejected: shipped `sweepIdle` wrote `expired` over a turn in flight after 2 h of silence, so the new design degrades no worse, and the mechanism lens owns turn-boundary correctness); filing DLQ Redis memory over 7-day holds (rejected: §12.4 and §17.8 state no Redis memory budget to breach, the DLQ caps at 500 entries per session, and **Refuted: the 7-day suspended population.** covers the population).
FACT: the leader re-check does not resume on a Redis error. `BacklogRechecker.Pass` logs a `HeldLen` error and writes nothing, so a Redis outage cannot cause a mass `suspended → resume_pending` stampede. The coordinator's `ResumeBacklog` returns true on a `HeldLen` error only to skip that tick's release, and it starts no resume. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 2 **`ResumeBacklog`.** and item 16.3
FACT: the watchdog `Tick` is serial on a 5 s ticker (pkg/gateway/runtime/watchdog/watchdog.go:166, :1243), and `SuspendIdle` calls `turnsQuiet` inline from `sweepIdle` under a 5 s deadline (non-spec CODE-6 items 5.3 and 18.5). Each over-idle `running` session whose adapter does not answer therefore stalls every other sweep on that replica for up to 5 s per tick. Only the coordinator queries, so the cost is bounded by the number of non-answering adapters among the over-idle sessions that replica coordinates. This is a code-only concern and is outside the spec loop.
WATCHOUT: for the non-spec performance or reliability lens, run `SuspendIdle`'s adapter query off `Tick`, as `ResumeBacklog` and `ReleaseSuspendedPod` already run their work, or bound the stall. Do not file it against the spec: the §4.7 `AttachTurnState` row's 5 s deadline is correct. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 2 **`ResumeBacklog`.** (its stated reason for using a goroutine) and item 5.3
WATCHOUT: non-spec-changes.md Edge cases **Turn state unavailable or never zero.** accepts that the `Idle` release can end an unrecorded delivery that reaches the adapter after the release's query, during a §12.3 failover. The caller's directive bars any accepted mid-turn release window. This sentence sits in non-spec text, not in the staged spec text, so the non-spec loop owns it. SPEC-5f states only "asks the adapter again and keeps the pod while a turn is outstanding" and accepts no window. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md line beginning "- **Turn state unavailable or never zero.**"
USEFUL [Standing context **Leader capacity.**]: the bound of about 10,000 rows per 300 s at Tier 3 saved re-deriving the leader pass cost.
USEFUL [Standing context **Refuted: the 7-day suspended population.**]: closed the per-replica `sweepSuspended` listing question.

### [restructure.non-spec-to-constraints]
DECISION: CODE-4 and CODE-6, and the Design paragraphs on the lease gate, the binding check, the delivery lock, the session-row read authority, and the message-path read failures, are restated as invariants (D1 to D5) with the files to touch, the named tests that pin each invariant, and bounded IMPLEMENTOR'S CHOICE. Item numbers and the sub-labels that tests, edge cases, CODE-3, the summary, and spec-changes cite are unchanged, except those [redesign9.reconcile.1] deletes: CODE-6 item 4 step 2a, item 5 sub-items 1 to 5, and item 18 sub-items 1, 4, and 5, with item 18's remaining sub-items renumbered 1 and 2. The restatement itself changes no behavior and removes no test obligation.
DECISION: the three read-authority rules collapse into one invariant: a read-pool row selects work and never decides a write, a one-shot decision with no write reads the primary, and a declined mutator returns a sentinel. How `ReadPrimary` reaches the primary is an IMPLEMENTOR'S CHOICE, bounded to write nothing and to hold the row lock for one round trip.
DECISION: the per-replica in-flight records of `DriveResume`, `ResumeBacklog`, and `ReleaseSuspendedPod`, the 60 s retry record, the attempt timer, the Redis commands behind `Peek`, `Ack`, `PeekOldest`, and `Remove`, and the `ListPodlessSuspended` query text are IMPLEMENTOR'S CHOICE with stated bounds.
DECISION: CODE-4 item 14 states a constraint on the Sweeper renew term and stages no code change.
FACT (moved rationale): today `Binder.Resume` mints no credentials, and `releaseEarlierBinding` revokes the session's leases through `Binder.Release`, so a checkpoint-restored runtime receives an empty credential file. This is why CODE-4 item 20 exists.
FACT (moved rationale): `rollbackBinding`, `Release`, `ReleaseSlot`, and `ReclaimClaimed` revoke every lease of the session, and the slot identifier is the session identifier. A session-wide release on an attempt's failure path could therefore revoke a later attempt's leases. This is why CODE-4 items 5.3, 20.4, and 24 release by identifier or by generation.
FACT (moved rationale): today `sweepResuming`'s mutator returns nil on a state miss, so the store advances `UpdatedAt` and re-anchors a fresh `resume_pending` window, and the sweep counts and notifies a retry that a failure report produced. `retriesRemain` read from a stale list can write `RetryCount` above `maxRetries`. This is why CODE-4 item 15 exists.
FACT (moved rationale): `PodExecutor.Send` returns a context error mid-turn after the runtime has consumed the message. This is why each held entry's send, record, and removal run on the server-lifetime context (CODE-4 item 6).
FACT (moved rationale): `executor.Send` waits for the runtime's reply to each turn, and `Watchdog.Run` calls `Tick` serially, so an inline backlog delivery, release, or idle suspension would stall every other sweep on the replica (CODE-6 items 2 and 4).
FACT (moved rationale): calling `deliverBuffered` inside `MaterializeDelegatedChild` would deliver a held message ahead of the task input (CODE-4 item 21, CODE-6 item 7).
FACT (moved rationale): an off-holder `deliverBuffered` would fail every `Send` in `streamFor` (`executor/pod.go`, "session %s is not bound to a pod") and strand the held messages of a `running` session. This is why the off-holder held-pod `/resume` fails closed (CODE-4 item 8).
FACT (moved rationale): today `applyFailureFromActive` takes `slotAccountLocks` only for a slot binding and releases it before `releaseReportedBinding`, so a same-replica attempt can claim, commit, and publish a replacement that the funnel's `releaseExecutor` then tears down (CODE-4 item 22).
FACT (moved rationale): today `credRenewalWiring.Renew` re-mints any tracked lease, including one that a suspension release, `ReleaseUncommitted`, `failResume`, or a session-end release returned (CODE-4 item 23).
FACT (moved rationale): a SCAN cursor is valid only on the node that issued it (CODE-6 item 14, `PurgeRoot`).

FACT: shipped §6.2 release step 3 retries a failed suspension checkpoint "on the next evaluation interval (60s)". ### [spec.12.review-performance.1]
DECISION: no performance or failure-mode finding in the round-12 spec staging. BECAUSE the r10-prefix delta has two edits and neither adds a store write, watch, RPC, or lock. SPEC-5f now reads "the gateway lifts the seal and writes nothing" on a checkpoint failure or a write miss, and SPEC-5i **Delivery of held messages.** cites SPEC-5f for the non-completion causes and no longer lists them. Under a Postgres failover the idle write repeats on a store error, and checkpoint retries stay paced by code at 60 s (see [spec.10.review-performance.1] FACT). ### [non-spec.8.fix-design-G2.1]
DECISION: CODE-6 item 4 `SuspendIdle` step 3 classifies a guard miss that follows a store error by the guard's row in three ways: `suspended`/`Idle`/empty pod counts as landed; `running` naming the pod the guard required did not land, so it unseals as a clean miss does; any other row, and a context end, keep the seal. "No store error lifts the seal." is deleted. BECAUSE a landed `Idle` write clears `PodAssignment`, and step 4 has not yet released the pod (it is still `bound`, so neither Idle-phase nor a reserved hold), so no resume can put that pod back on the row. SPEC-5f "the write misses its condition ... lifts the seal" therefore binds that branch. ALTERNATIVES: keep the seal on every post-error miss and narrow SPEC-5f (rejected: this loop is non-spec, and the `running`+same-pod outcome is known, so keeping the seal is an unnecessary up-to-900 s DLQ detour); unseal on every post-error miss (rejected: a landed-then-resumed row on a fresh pod would lose the seal that keeps the old, still-bound pod's runtime turn-free until the orphan-claim GC reclaims it).
FACT: in the remaining "other miss" rows (an interrupt suspension, a terminal state, or recovery onto another pod) the session is no longer `running` on the sealed pod, so the kept seal is harmless there. Only the context-end case can leave a sealed `running` session, and that is the outcome SPEC-5f's "A seal the gateway does not lift" sentence covers. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 4 step 3; pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podclaim/claimer.go `claimIdle` (Idle phase only) and `rebindReserved`.
FACT: an `UnsealSession` that reaches a newer registry entry is harmless, because a new entry starts unsealed and a fenced newer generation answers `coordinator_handoff_stale`. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md **Session seal.** Handlers.
CORRECTS [review-log WATCHOUTs and USEFUL at the ledger entries quoting "No store error lifts the seal" (round-7 spec WATCHOUT, the r-12 USEFUL, and the "keyed on the write's true outcome" WATCHOUT)]: a post-store-error miss on a `running` row that still names the guarded pod is a known non-landing and lifts the seal. Only the other post-error misses, and a context end, keep it.
WATCHOUT: the discriminating test is the store wrapper that errors WITHOUT applying, after which `LastAgentActivityAt` moves. A plain guard miss with no prior error passes under both readings. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md Tests that land with CODE-6, tier-1 session server bullet.

### [spec.13.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: The adapter carries the turn count through a checkpoint: each checkpoint records the peak count during capture with the session file, and a `Resume`-created entry starts at the recorded count (0 when no session file is restored). The one normative home is SPEC-5ab item 2 **Session seal.**, and CODE-6 item 18.3 **Checkpoint record.** carries constraints only. BECAUSE a restored runtime continues an in-flight turn with no new `message` (spec/08_recursive-delegation.md **Duplicate spawn across parent recovery.**, spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:426-428), so a zero start lets an idle firing seal and release mid-turn. ALTERNATIVES: a ready_for_input gate (no carrier for the signal, so it disables idle suspension on every resumed session); starting at 1 (sticks forever after a between-turns restore); settling on the first `response` (responses carry no correlation); proto fields plus a checkpoint column (new wire surface for adapter-internal state); a runtime `continuing` flag (changes the runtime contract); accepting the window (caller directive forbids it).
WATCHOUT: The record must precede the session file in archive stream order, so a tail-truncated partial reassembly that restores the file also restores the record, and it must sit outside `/sessions/{sessionId}` or any other runtime-writable directory, because a runtime that forges it to zero reopens a mid-turn release. Do not add a decay or timeout to a stuck restored count: `maxSessionAge` bounds it, and that is the fail-safe direction. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 18.3.
FACT: The idle suspension's own checkpoint is taken under the seal at count 0, so the normal suspend-then-resume path records 0 and seals again normally after resume. EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md SPEC-5ab item 2 (`SealSession` seals only at count 0).

Check whether the step's file or test enumeration needs those names.

### [spec.13.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: close the Resume-created zero-count gap by carrying the count through the checkpoint: each checkpoint records, with the session file, the highest count the session held while it was captured, and a `Resume`-created entry starts at the count recorded with the session file it restores (zero when it restores none). One clause plus one sentence in SPEC-5ab item 2, plus a CODE-6 item 18 sub-item and one tier-1 test. — BECAUSE the spec does establish autonomous continuation of an in-flight turn after a restore (spec/08_recursive-delegation.md **Duplicate spawn across parent recovery.**: "re-issues any `delegate_task` call whose tool result is absent"; spec/07_session-lifecycle.md **External side effects across recovery.**), so the finding is valid; the adapter alone knows the count at checkpoint time and alone restores the archive, so no proto, column, or gateway change is needed. — ALTERNATIVES: (1) the reviewer's gate on `ready_for_input` since the `Resume` (rejected: the carrier of that signal is `unstated`, spec/29_communication-scenarios.md step 8 near :482, and the code defers it, pkg/gateway/sessionserver/resume_held_pod.go:58-59; built literally, every entry a `Resume` created refuses every seal, so a session resumed once from a podless suspension never idle-suspends again); (2) start every `Resume`-created entry at one (rejected: a restore from a between-turns checkpoint, the common case, never sees the extra `response`, so the count sticks at one forever on that entry); (3) settle a resumed entry on its first `response` (rejected: `response` frames carry no message correlation, spec/28_communication-channels.md **Outbound: `response`**, so a hidden turn's `response` and a new message's `response` cannot be told apart; a message arriving mid-continuation gets sealed mid-turn); (4) a `turn_outstanding` field on `CheckpointSummary` and `ResumeRequest` with a checkpoint-row column (rejected: two wire fields and a column for state the adapter can carry in its own archive); (5) a runtime-declared `continuing` flag on `session_started` (rejected: runtime contract change for every runtime and conformance battery).
FACT: the idle suspension's own checkpoint is taken under the seal at count 0 with no `message` writable, so the main idle-suspend → resume path records 0 and is unaffected; the fix only changes restores from periodic, eviction, drain, rotation, and interrupt-release checkpoints. EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md SPEC-5f **Idle suspension.** ("Once the session is sealed, the gateway checkpoints")
FACT: `response` frames carry only `type`, `output`, `sessionId`; no message correlation exists on CH-MSGSOCK. EVIDENCE: spec/28_communication-channels.md **Outbound: `response`** (~:753-767)
FACT: the session file is captured from the runtime-writable `/sessions/{sessionId}` tmpfs under `workspace.SessionsPrefix` (pkg/adapter/slot.go:493-525, pkg/adapter/server.go:85-93); a count record placed there is forgeable by the runtime toward 0, which would reopen a mid-turn release.
WATCHOUT: a runtime that does not continue a restored in-flight turn leaves a recorded count of 1 stuck on that entry, so every idle firing is refused and `maxSessionAge` bounds the session (SPEC-5f refusal outcome). This is the fail-safe direction; do not "fix" it by decaying the count or by a timeout, which reopens the mid-turn release. EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md SPEC-5f
WATCHOUT: record the count before the session file in the archive's stream order, or a tail-truncated partial reassembly can restore a session file without its record and start the entry at zero mid-turn. EVIDENCE: spec/28_communication-channels.md CH-OBJSTORE row (partial reassembly)
CORRECTS [review-log line ~1106 WATCHOUT on the Session seal count]: the spec does establish autonomous continuation after a restore; §8.10 **Duplicate spawn across parent recovery.** says the restored parent re-issues any `delegate_task` whose result is absent from the checkpoint. The filing it declined is valid.

### [spec.13.review-performance.1]
DECISION: no performance or failure-mode finding in the round-13 spec staging — BECAUSE the redesign-10 delta (SPEC-5f generation conjunct on the suspend write and no unseal on a generation miss, SPEC-5ab as the home of the unlifted-seal bound, SPEC-5e counting a client message once the adapter writes it) adds no store write, watch, lock, or RPC. The conjunct rides the existing one-row `Update`; a generation miss leaves the seal, and the next 5 s watchdog firing on the current coordinator re-seals (count stays 0) and completes, so a takeover or a Redis-lease-loss re-adoption costs at most one extra tick. During a Postgres outage no takeover can increment the generation (spec/10_gateway-internals.md §10.1.1 Postgres-unavailable item 1), so the conjunct cannot strand an in-flight suspension then — ALTERNATIVES: (1) filing messages refused by a left seal waiting in the DLQ until the next idle firing (rejected: latency trade-off already on the refuted list, bounded by `maxSessionAge`); (2) filing Redis loss of those held messages (rejected: Standing **Refuted: store-outage degradation.**); (3) filing the per-qualifying-event `last_agent_activity_at` stamp as new write load (rejected: SPEC-5e only moves the stamp point from receipt to adapter write; the per-event Postgres stamp predates 0092).
FACT: §10.1.2 step 1 CAS precedes step 2 `CoordinatorFence`, so SPEC-5f's "advances `coordination_generation` before the adopting coordinator sends the pod any RPC" holds. EVIDENCE: spec/10_gateway-internals.md:37-38
USEFUL [non-spec.11.review-performance.1]: its FACT that watchdog and Sweeper already full-scan rows per tick spared re-deriving the podless-population cost.

### [spec.13.review-reliability.1]
DECISION: no reliability findings in spec round 13 — BECAUSE crash, store-error, and takeover paths through the redesign-10 idle suspension (SPEC-5f, SPEC-5ab) all end in a bounded state. (1) A crash between seal and write leaves the seal. The peer adopts the `running` row (SPEC-2a). Refused messages do not reset `last_agent_activity_at` (SPEC-5e), so the adopter's next idle firing re-seals at count 0 and completes. (2) A crash after the write leaves the pod unreferenced, and orphan-claim GC reclaims it. The leader re-check covers the backlog, and in-memory inbox loss is already accepted. (3) A stale replica's late `UnsealSession` after a takeover cannot lift the adopter's seal, because the pod rejects any gateway-to-pod RPC with a stale generation. — ALTERNATIVES: filing a stale replica's checkpoint-failure unseal racing the adopter's suspension (rejected: generation fencing on every pod RPC); filing the interrupt hold release (SPEC-5b), which has no generation conjunct (rejected: the row is `suspended`, so no delivery is made, and SPEC-1f item 3 covers a release by a replica that lost the lease); filing messages held behind a seal that was not lifted (rejected: latency bounded by the next idle firing or `maxSessionAge`, already refuted).
FACT: the pod validates `coordination_generation` on every gateway-to-pod RPC and rejects a stale one, so `SealSession`/`UnsealSession` from a replica that lost the session are refused once the adopter's `CoordinatorFence` lands — EVIDENCE: spec/28_communication-channels.md:237-238
FACT: concurrent idle attempts on one replica at one generation are excluded by the per-replica in-flight record that `SuspendIdle` shares with `ReleaseSuspendedPod` — EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 4 **`SuspendIdle`.** ("when a release or an idle suspension of the session is in flight on this replica")
USEFUL [Standing **Refuted: store-outage degradation.**]: it saved refiling the loss of `suspended` DLQ entries held in Redis for 7 days.

### [spec.14.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: Each checkpoint archive carries one turn record (`adapter/turns`, last entry); the leading record (`adapter/turns-lead`) is deleted. A restore that read chunks but no record sets per-entry `turnsUnknown`, and `SealSession` refuses while it is set — BECAUSE a record written before the session file finishes archiving cannot bound the `message` frames that file holds, so any count taken from it admits a mid-turn seal and contradicts SPEC-5f — ALTERNATIVES: holding `message` writes from the leading record until the session file is archived (second mechanism, blocking wait with wake-up on every capture abort path); flooring the count at 1 (unsound: several post-lead messages drain it to 0 mid-turn); accepting the omission (the excluded mid-turn window).
WATCHOUT: Do not reintroduce a leading turn record or a count floor for a cut restore; do not encode the refusal as a sentinel count (a later `response` decrements it). A `Resume` with no chunks starts at 0 and is not a cut restore. maxSessionAge bounds the refusal. — EVIDENCE: spec-changes SPEC-5ab **Session seal.**; non-spec CODE-6 item 18.3.
CORRECTS [standing context, Session seal trap paragraph]: "Keep both turn records and their order" is withdrawn; there is one turn record, and a restore cut before it refuses the seal.
FACT: Today the refusal is unreachable: `ExtractTree` errors on a truncated stream (pkg/adapter/workspace/tree.go:170) and `Resume` aborts (pkg/adapter/resume.go:243); RECORDS-1 7(s) files it. — EVIDENCE: those lines.

### [spec.14.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: Delete the leading turn record. The archive carries one turn record, as its last entry; `Resume` sets the count from it, to zero when no archive is restored, and when the restored archive ends before the record (a §10.1.7 **Reassembly on resume.** end-truncated restore) the adapter refuses every `SealSession` for that entry, so `maxSessionAge` bounds it — BECAUSE no record written before the session file ends can bound the `message` frames that file holds, so any count read from a pre-session-file record admits a mid-turn seal; refusing the seal is the existing fail-safe outcome of "a turn the runtime never answers" — ALTERNATIVES: (a) the reviewer's write hold from the leading record until the session file is archived: a new blocking wait on the message path with wake-up obligations on every capture abort path, stalling delivery for the length of the session-file archive on every checkpoint, to serve a restore path the tree cannot even run today (RECORDS-1 7(s)); (b) the count floored at 1 on a cut restore: unsound, because several `message` frames can be written after the leading record and the runtime answers them in order, so the count reaches 0 mid-turn.
FACT: `ExtractTree` returns an error on any read failure and `Resume` aborts on it, so no partial-workspace restore runs in the tree; the refusal costs nothing until RECORDS-1 7(s) is fixed. EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/workspace/tree.go:170, pkg/adapter/resume.go:243.
CORRECTS [spec.13 WATCHOUT "The record must precede the session file in archive stream order"]: a record that precedes the session file does not bound the frames the file holds; the record is the archive's last entry, and a restore cut before it refuses the seal. The half of that WATCHOUT about the record sitting outside any runtime-writable directory, and about adding no decay to a stuck count, stays true.
WATCHOUT: Distinguish "no archive" (count 0) from "an archive cut before its record" (seal refused) in `Resume`: both see found=false from `ExtractTree`, and only the second restored chunks. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 18.3.

### [spec.14.mechanism-respec.turn-count.1]
DECISION: the turn count crosses a checkpoint as metadata. CheckpointSummary.turn_count goes to checkpoint_manifest.turn_count (partial=false only, migration 0184; derive copies the parent's) and then to ResumeRequest.turn_count. Resume sets the count; no count with chunks means unknown, which refuses the seal until the next `response` — BECAUSE the archive record needed a stream-order rule, a peak, a capture flag, and a goroutine join, and it still could not cover a truncated archive. A metadata field written once at completion has no ordering and is absent on every partial row by construction — ALTERNATIVES: the trailing archive record of [spec.14.fix-design-G1.1] (rejected: those four mechanisms and the `adapter/` entry exposed through GET /workspace); a count read before the capture (rejected: undercounts `message` frames that the restored file holds); a peak over the capture carried as metadata (open decision OD-1 of this redesign; default not taken).

FACT: the tree has no turn count today. The finalise and resume sites the carriage touches are uploadDriver.onSummary and finaliseAbort (pkg/gateway/checkpoint/checkpointer/uploaddriver.go), deriveChunkedCheckpoint (pkg/gateway/sessionserver/derive.go), Store.Finalise and MemoryStore.Finalise (partialmanifeststore.go), pgstore.Store.Finalise, sessionserver.CheckpointManifestWriter (checkpoint_seams.go), resumechunks.Resolve, resolveResumeChunks and resolveFullCheckpointFallback (resume_checkpoint.go), checkpointResumeRequest (resume_rebind.go), Binder.Resume (podsession/resume.go), adapterclient.Client.Resume, and the adapter's Resume (pkg/adapter/resume.go, restoreChunks before Runtime.Start). Finalise also has seven test callers outside the store packages; CODE-6 item 18.3 names them.
WATCHOUT: do not move the count back into the archive, and do not read it on any path other than the end of the archive stream. A Finalise caller other than onSummary and derive passes nil.

### [spec.16.review-reliability.1]
DECISION: no reliability findings on the staged spec edits in round 16. BECAUSE every crash, restart, and failover path through the redesign-12 turn-count carriage ends in a known count or in an unknown count, and an unknown count only refuses the seal. Paths traced: a gateway crash between the adapter's terminal summary and `Finalise` (the row is never finalised `partial = false`, so the restore passes no count and the count is unknown); a finalise that fails during a Postgres failover (the selector restores an older complete row, whose count and archive are a pair); legacy rows written before migration 0184 (NULL, so unknown); a held-pod resume and a `CoordinatorFence` takeover (the registry entry and its count survive, and no `Resume` runs); a snapshotless rebuild and a no-archive restore (count 0, with no carried conversation). The idle seal also ends bounded when `SealSession` times out after the seal landed, or when `UnsealSession` fails after a `last_agent_activity_at` miss: the seal stays until the next idle firing re-seals and completes, and refused messages do not reset the idle clock (SPEC-5e). ALTERNATIVES: filing the 7-day Redis-only DLQ hold for `suspended` against the Postgres-backed `session_dlq_archive` that `awaiting_client_action` gets (rejected: Standing **Refuted: store-outage degradation.** and **Not filed** `session_dlq_archive` replay); filing an unspecified backoff for the driver's pre-claim retries (rejected: the spec states that it retries later and that §7.3 step 3c bounds the wait, and the non-spec Testing pins a jittered backoff); filing derive's start path for a mid-turn parent (rejected: speculative, and the derive count copy is non-spec and already an OPEN).
FACT: §7.2 delivery path 1 resolves a `lenny/request_input` answer directly and writes no stdin `message`, so `input_required` answers never move the adapter's turn count. EVIDENCE: spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:326
FACT: §4.4.5's minimal state record resume (`conversation_only`) restores no archive, so under SPEC-5ab its count starts at 0. The record holds only the last completed prompt/response pair, and the driver has no minimal-state branch (RECORDS-1 7(q)). EVIDENCE: spec/04_system-components.md:284-292
USEFUL [spec.13.review-reliability.1]: its seal-crash trace (seal left by a crashed attempt, re-seal on the adopter's idle firing, and a stale unseal refused by generation fencing) still holds after redesign 12. Re-verifying it took one read.
USEFUL [spec.15.review-fresh.1]: its WATCHOUT on the §10.1.7 in-pod fallback, which yields an unknown count rather than an unsafe one, saved a refile.

DECISION: no performance or failure-mode finding this round — BECAUSE each new per-message cost is small against the stated budgets: two Redis peeks and one primary read per path-2 message, against about 3,000 req/s at Tier 3 and a Redis budget of about 100k ops/s (spec/17 §17.8; spec/12 §12.4). Idle-suspension claim churn is at most about 11 extra claims/s at 10,000 sessions and a 900 s idle bound, against the 30/s claim profile in the §4.6.1 etcd table. The leader re-check, `sweepSuspended`, and the Sweeper skip are bounded as Settled states. — ALTERNATIVES: filing ReadPrimary-as-`FOR UPDATE` WAL amplification was rejected. It is an IMPLEMENTOR'S CHOICE example, and the message path already makes a per-event `AdvanceLastSeq` row write, which costs more.

### [non-spec.16.review-performance.1]
DECISION: no performance or failure-mode finding in non-spec round 16 — BECAUSE the r14-prefix delta only moves the `resumeHeldPod` not-`suspended` PreconditionError wrap from CODE-6 item 6 into CODE-4 item 8 and adds `resume_held_pod.go` to CODE-4 Targets; it adds no store write, Redis call, RPC, watch, or lock. A whole read of CODE-4, CODE-5, and CODE-6 under this lens found nothing new: the turn count rides the existing manifest finalise UPDATE and resume-selection read, and it lives in adapter memory, so it survives a coordinator handoff and a Redis reset. `HeldLen` errors during a Redis outage only defer an interrupt-hold release. The shipped watchdog never releases a held pod (`MaxSuspendedPodHoldSeconds` is read only by config defaulting, pkg/gateway/runtime/watchdog/watchdog.go:197-250), so that deferral is no regression — ALTERNATIVES: (1) the unpaced `SuspendIdle` step-3 and `completeResume` commit repeats during a Postgres failover (rejected: Traps **Commit repeat pacing.**, refuted many times); (2) `CREATE INDEX` without CONCURRENTLY in migration 0183, and the CHECK-validating ADD COLUMN in 0182 and 0184 (rejected: no spec or repo migration rule requires online DDL, only 0156 uses CONCURRENTLY, and the platform has no deployments); (3) a restore from a mid-turn periodic checkpoint pinning a pod until maxSessionAge (rejected: accepted in the spec Edge cases bullet **A turn the runtime never answers.**, and pinned by `TestRestoreFromMidTurnCheckpointNotIdleSuspended_spec_4_7_1`); (4) per-replica `DriveResume` lease reads for each `resume_pending` row on each 5 s tick (rejected: the population is transient and bounded by the resume window, and the rate is far inside the ~100k ops/s Redis budget).
FACT: the watchdog is not leader-gated. Every replica runs `Tick` over every tenant and lists each state with its own `List` (pkg/gateway/runtime/watchdog/watchdog.go:588-666), so a per-row call that a new sweep adds runs once per replica per tick unless D2 (the local-binding check) returns first. Check D2 ordering before costing any new per-row call. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/runtime/watchdog/watchdog.go:588-666, cmd/lenny-gateway/controlserver.go:221

### [non-spec.19.review-reliability.1]
DECISION: no findings under the reliability lens in non-spec round 19 — BECAUSE the r17-prefix delta is one sentence (CODE-4 item 8: on `errResumeHeldPodNotSuspended`, call `enterResumePending` with the read row's `State` set to `awaiting_client_action`). The delivery lock and D1 keep the other held-pod writers off the row, so the guarded write admits only an `awaiting_client_action` row (200 `resume_pending`) and answers 409 for anything else. The tier-1 `handleResume` case pins both outcomes. A whole trace of the turn count found no release with a turn in flight outside the SPEC-5ab windows. The trace covered the Checkpoint summary read after `ArchiveTree`, `onSummary` -> `Finalise(partial=false)`, the partial row with a nil count, `Resolve` reading the row it grants, the `LatestFull` and ref fallbacks, and the adapter `Resume`, the only Resume caller, which always runs on a freshly claimed entry — ALTERNATIVES: the `session_state` drain label taking `awaiting_client_action` from the overwritten row (label only, not correctness); per-tick `SealSession` RPCs for a session that holds a turn outstanding forever (performance lens, and the no-retry-time rule was already refuted).
FACT: the adapter `Resume` handler is reached only from `podsession.Binder.Resume` (`resume.go:152`) through `resumeOnPod`'s checkpoint branch (`resume_rebind.go:102`). No coordinator-handoff path sends `Resume` to a live entry, so the item 18.3 reset ("turns = 0 when no chunks") never zeroes the count of a session already running — EVIDENCE: grep of `.Resume(` under pkg/gateway and cmd/lenny-gateway; pkg/adapter/resume.go:44-50 comment mentions a "coordinator-handoff resume" that no caller sends.
FACT: `resumechunks.Resolve` reads the manifest row through `Manifests.Get` before it mints grants, so taking `TurnCount` from "the row whose grants they return" needs no extra read — EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/checkpoint/resumechunks/resumechunks.go:120-121.

DECISION: no security finding this round. BECAUSE every bound I traced has a trusted, durable source: active session age accrues in the Postgres store funnel (CODE-1), the retry count and suspended lifetime (`SuspendedAt`) are Postgres columns, D1 fails closed when the lease read fails, and the off-holder held-pod `/resume` fails closed with `TARGET_NOT_READY`. The count also bounds no cross-session or cross-tenant property.

The adopter's `CoordinatorFence` makes the stale replica's step-2 checkpoint fail at the adapter, and the row guard (suspended, same `SuspendedAt`, same pod) loses to any adopter write that leaves `suspended`. Only the idle write needs the generation conjunct. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 4 step 3; settled **Release guard.**

The tier-9 `TestResumedSessionAuthenticatesWithFreshLease` asserts that the old proxy token is rejected after the idle release (non-spec-changes.md Tier 9 bullet).

### [spec.17.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: an unaddressed `heartbeat_ack` is attributed to no session for the seal (SPEC-5ab item 2); it still answers liveness — BECAUSE the adapter writes each heartbeat on one stream naming one session, so a bare ack says nothing about a streamless co-tenant, and attributing it to every session let that co-tenant pass the no-ack refusal and be sealed mid-work — ALTERNATIVES: attribute to sessions heartbeated since the last ack (new per-entry state, closes nothing more); attribute only on a single-slot pod (compatibility path); make `sessionId` Required=Yes on the ack (forces SDK, tier-1, tier-3 churn; a bare ack is harmless once it attributes nothing).
WATCHOUT: do not reintroduce "attributed to every session on the pod" for bare acks; a runtime that acks bare is refused every seal and `maxSessionAge` bounds it, which is the intended fail-closed outcome. CODE-6 item 18 `observeRuntimeFrame` and `TestActivityClockStampsEveryFrame_spec_4_7_1` now assert a bare ack sets nothing — EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/attach.go:318-323 passes an unaddressed ack to every stream's liveness monitor, which is a separate behavior.
FACT: the SPEC-5ab activity bullet for runtime frames no longer cites §28.5.3 **Addressing.** (that rule resolves only against the delivering stream); it states the `deliverToSession` resolution directly: `sessionId` names the session, or no `sessionId` on a pod with at most one slot — EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/attach.go:376-395.
FACT: SPEC-5ab item 4 now carries two edits to the §28.5.1 CH-ATTACH **Timing.** bullet: the seal deadline sentence and the stream-lifetime pointer to §6.2 **Idle suspension.** for the earlier opening — EVIDENCE: spec/28_communication-channels.md:241-242.

### [spec.17.review-performance.1]
DECISION: no performance or failure-mode finding in the spec-round-17 staging (redesign 13: `busy` on `heartbeat_ack`, OD-S1 cap exemption, resume admission) — BECAUSE the new costs are small at Tier 3/4: a busy or `type: mcp` session costs one `SealSession` RPC plus one `last_agent_activity_at` write per idle window (10,000/900 s ≈ 11/s at Tier 3, ≈ 111/s at Tier 4), and SPEC-5f re-arms the clock one window out on every outcome, so nothing re-asks on each 5 s tick. Per-session heartbeats stay inside the pod. The admission check runs only on exits from `suspended`, and with every cap at its default of 0 it issues no query. Under a §12.3 primary failover the message hold path already fails at its primary re-read (**Enqueue racing a terminal transition.**), so the primary-only count queries add no new outage — ALTERNATIVES: (1) the leader re-check's per-pass cost over an uncapped podless population (rejected for this loop: the existing per-replica watchdog and Sweeper full scans dominate it, per [non-spec.11.review-performance.1]); (2) held-pod `suspended` sessions escaping the per-user cap (rejected: the owner decided OD-S1 "with or without its pod", summary.md:43).
CORRECTS [Standing context **Leader capacity.**]: the podless `suspended` population is no longer bounded by the concurrent-session caps. SPEC-6a exempts `suspended` from every cap, and the caps default to 0 anyway (spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:1111 "the cap defaults to 0, disabled"). The bound is now creation rate × time to expiry: §16.5 Tier 3 sustains 200 creations/s (spec/16_observability.md:596), and the time to expiry is `maxSuspendedSessionSeconds` (604800 s) plus one idle window. About 84 times more abandoned sessions stay non-terminal than under the 7200 s idle termination.
CORRECTS [Standing context **Refuted: the 7-day suspended population.**]: its premise "bounded by the caps" no longer holds after OD-S1. The leader pass is still small next to the pre-existing full scans, but the Sweeper's per-row `leases.Get` over podless rows (every replica, every 15 s) now scales with the 7-day population.
DEFERRED [non-spec-changes.md]: CODE-7 item 1 says the new count predicate `state NOT IN (terminal…, 'suspended')` "implies the migration-0102 partial-index predicate, so no migration is added". The implication is true, but 0102 indexes only `(tenant_id)` WHERE non-terminal (migrations/0102_sessions_active_by_tenant_index.up.sql:17-19), and `state` is not an index column. So every creation and resume COUNT must fetch from the heap every `suspended` row of the tenant (or of all tenants for the global cap) to exclude it, and that population is now 7-day and uncapped. What is true instead: the count needs a partial index whose predicate also excludes `suspended`, or one that includes `state`. Owner: the non-spec performance lens.
OPEN: under OD-S1 "with or without its pod", a user at the per-user cap can hold more pods by repeatedly creating a session and interrupting it, each pod held up to `maxSuspendedPodHoldSeconds` (900 s) uncounted. Only the creation rate limit and the namespace ResourceQuota bound this. A human should confirm the owner intended the held-pod half of the exemption.
FACT: every `CountActiveSessions*` query runs on the primary pool (`s.pool`), not the read pool — EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/session/sessionstore/pgstore/pgstore.go:862, :885, :909, :931
USEFUL [non-spec.11.review-performance.1]: its WATCHOUT about pre-existing full scans settled which side of the bar the uncapped-population leader cost falls on.

### [spec.17.review-security.1]
FACT: The concurrent-session counts the resume admission check reuses are Postgres COUNTs over the sessions table, so they need no Redis durable fallback. Per-tenant uses `CountActiveSessions`, and per-user, per-runtime, and global use `CountActive*`. A counter error fails closed with 500. — EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/quota.go:41, :185-218
FACT: The §11.1 control table lists a per-team concurrency scope, but no limit surface exists for it in code, so SPEC-6a can omit it from the resume check without leaving a gate open. — EVIDENCE: spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:8; pkg/gateway/sessionserver/quota.go:168-172
FACT: `busy` on `heartbeat_ack` is a runtime self-report, but it bounds no security property. It only defers idle suspension, and `maxSessionAge` is gateway-measured active time that accrues while `running`, so it still bounds the session. Do not file it under the pod-self-report bar.
FACT: The SPEC-1g3 renewal check fails closed on a store error. Per non-spec CODE-4 item 23, a `Lookup` error is retried rather than treated as a released lease, and it never triggers a renewal of a released lease.
OPEN: OD-S9 (an open owner decision, not filed here): the failure edge out of a held-pod `suspended` session can be triggered by the session's own runtime crashing during an interrupt hold. Suspended sessions are exempt from the caps, so the number of sessions that can take this unchecked re-entry is bounded only by the hold window and pool capacity, not by the in-flight concurrency that SPEC-6a **Concurrent admissions.** suggests. The owner may want that stated when deciding OD-S9.
DECISION: no security findings on the staged spec edits — BECAUSE the held-pod cap exemption is owner decision OD-S1 (summary item 27, "with or without its pod"), every suspended→running/resume_pending write in SPEC-5i/SPEC-6a carries the admission check, and no edit adds pod RBAC, egress, or a webhook dependency — ALTERNATIVES: filing the failure-edge bypass was rejected as an open decision's framing.

### [spec.21.review-performance.1]
DECISION: no performance or failure-mode finding in the spec-round-21 staging — BECAUSE the only top-tier cost that grows is the gateway leader's backlog re-check over the uncapped 7-day podless `suspended` population (Tier 3: ~1.2M rows per 1% of 200 creations/s that end idle; one Redis `HeldLen` per row per 300 s), and the shipped watchdog and Sweeper already list every session row, terminal rows included, on every replica each tick, so the leader pass adds no new O(rows) scan; the SealSession RPC plus one `last_agent_activity_at` write per idle window (~11/s Tier 3) and in-pod per-session heartbeats are negligible; under a Postgres failover, a Redis reset, or a coordinator handoff nothing staged degrades below the shipped design (podless rows hold no lease; held messages share the DLQ's pre-existing Redis-loss exposure) — ALTERNATIVES: filing the leader pass as a single-leader bottleneck (rejected, same ground as [spec.17.review-performance.1] and [non-spec.11.review-performance.1]: dominated by pre-existing full scans, and the spec does not forbid pipelining).

The pass cost is then (held rows) x (suspended rows) per 300 s. A partial index excluding `suspended` (or including `state`) in CODE-7 fixes both. Owner: non-spec performance lens.

### [spec.23.review-reliability.1]
FACT: The heartbeat-hung refusal of a later `Attach` is `DeadlineExceeded` in CODE-6 item 18, so it falls under the landed §28.5.1 **Degradation.** stream-failure rule ("ends a session's stream with `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` when the runtime misses its heartbeat ack"); SPEC-5ac item 7 does not need to name the status. — EVIDENCE: spec/28_communication-channels.md:256-258; non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 18 ("ends the stream with `DeadlineExceeded`")
FACT: Checkpoint-failure retry pacing for both the idle attempt and the interrupt release is the 60 s per-replica retry record in CODE-6 item 4 step 1 and `SuspendIdle`; the spec's "writes nothing and releases nothing" leaves the clock fired, so this pacing is what keeps a checkpoint-store outage from re-checkpointing every tick. It lives in code, so it is not a spec finding. — EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 4 steps 1-2
FACT: A `HeldLen` error skips the release on that tick (`ResumeBacklog` returns true) and the leader pass logs and goes on. A Redis outage therefore resumes nothing in bulk. — EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 2 ("On a `HeldLen` error it logs and returns true, so the row gets no release this tick"), item 16
DECISION: no findings in round 23 under the reliability lens — BECAUSE I traced each restart, failover, and redelivery path the staged spec adds (driver entry and commit, resuming watchdog, generation-scoped lease release, idle seal, write, and release, release-time migration, backlog resume at the coordinator, releaser, and leader, podless terminate, and admission refusal). Each one has a guard or a reclaimer, or matches an accepted Settled/Trap entry. — ALTERNATIVES: filing the orphaned-seal stall after a takeover (a client attach resets the gateway clock, which the SPEC-5e client-interaction bullet still lists, so the stall lasts one idle window after the last attach) was rejected because that recovery is only slower and SPEC-5ab already bounds it

### [spec.23.review-security.1]
DECISION: no security findings in spec round 23 — BECAUSE every bound the staging touches is sourced from a trusted durable store or a gateway measurement: the concurrent caps are Postgres COUNTs (SPEC-6a), the suspended lifetime and maxSessionAge accrue from session-row timestamps, budget-key expiry fails closed (spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:408-414), and `busy` or the adapter's idle answer decides only pod retention under the gateway-measured maxSessionAge — ALTERNATIVES: filing the unchecked failure edge out of `suspended` as a cap bypass by a crashing tenant runtime was rejected, because OD-S9 (Decision 27) settles it and SPEC-6a **Concurrent admissions.** states the overshoot.
FACT: Renewal after a pod release fails closed on a store error. A `LeaseStore.Lookup` error is retried and mints nothing, and only a confirmed missing record returns `ErrLeaseReleased`, so SPEC-1g3 needs no read-failure clause — EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-4 item 23.2 (`pgstore` reports missing only on `pgx.ErrNoRows`).
FACT: §6.2 graceful release step 2 currently says "releases the pod back to the pool" (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:229). SPEC-5b narrows it to the pool's session-end disposition, so a non-recycling pod drains. That tightens one-session-only reuse; it does not regress it.
FACT: The `PreMessageDelivery` phase is defined as firing "before the gateway delivers" an inter-session message (spec/04_system-components.md:1148). Running it at acceptance, before the DLQ hold, satisfies it for messages held to a `suspended` target.
WATCHOUT: `sessionPolicy.maxSessionRetries` deletion leaves §7.3 "bounded by deployer caps" (spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:386) and §11.2 "deployer-capped" with no named cap in spec. The code cap is `--retry-max-retries`. This is below the security bar (a resource budget whose deletion removes no reader); do not refile under security.

### [spec.27.fix-G1.1]
DECISION: SPEC-5ac item 8 (§15.7 **Busy reporting.**) pending window now runs "from reading a `message` for the session until its handler has returned and the SDK has written any response the handler produced" — BECAUSE the Go SDK answers `heartbeat` inline on the frame loop while the handler runs on the session goroutine and the response is written after `OnMessage` returns, so a handler-return endpoint left an ack-before-response that fails the §15.4.6 **heartbeat busy** row — ALTERNATIVES: "until the SDK finishes handling it" (ambiguous for a streaming non-final turn under the hold); response-write-only endpoint (streaming non-final writes no response, stuck busy until session_end).
FACT: Go SDK answers heartbeat inline in the frame loop and runs handlers on a per-session goroutine; response written after the handler returns — EVIDENCE: sdks/runtime/go/runtime/runtime.go (heartbeat ack write in the frame loop; response write after p.handler.OnMessage), sdks/runtime/go/runtime/session.go (`go p.serve(st)`).
WATCHOUT: the window's end is the conjunction "handler returned AND any response written"; do not drop either half. Response-only reintroduces the round-26 stuck-busy defect; handler-return-only reintroduces this round's ack-before-response gap. The busy-hold sentence ("after its handler returns") stays as is because writing the response is SDK work. — EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md SPEC-5ac item 8; non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 18.4 already decrements after writing the response.

### [spec.27.fix-design-G1.1]
DECISION: §15.7 **Busy reporting.** (SPEC-5ac item 8) ends the pending-message window "until its handler has returned and the SDK has written any response the handler produced", replacing "its handler has not yet returned" — BECAUSE the Go SDK answers `heartbeat` inline on the frame loop while the handler runs on the session goroutine and writes the `response` after `OnMessage` returns, so a handler-return endpoint leaves an idle-reading ack before the response, failing the §15.4.6 **heartbeat busy** row — ALTERNATIVES: bare "until the SDK finishes handling it" (rejected: round 26 made the SDK's handling end at handler return for a streaming non-final turn, so the phrase is ambiguous there); tying the window to the response write alone (rejected: a streaming non-final handler writes none and the count would stick until session_end, the trap summary line 56 records).
WATCHOUT: the window has two endpoints joined by "and": handler return AND the SDK's own write of whatever response it produced. Dropping either half reintroduces one of the two recorded failures (round 26: stuck busy on streaming non-final; round 27: idle ack before response). EVIDENCE: sdks/runtime/go/runtime/runtime.go (heartbeat answered inline; response written after p.handler.OnMessage returns), sdks/runtime/go/runtime/session.go (`go p.serve(st)`).

### [non-spec.21.fix-G1.1]
CORRECTS [round-20 WATCHOUT "start the subprocess reader only for a `spawnedByStart` child"]: spawn origin does not separate the two stdout readers. `Send` reuses a Start-spawned child (`session` returns the published child from `e.procs`) and scans the same pipe via `sess.stdout`. WATCHOUT: TestSubprocessExecutorStartSpawnsProcess, TestSubprocessStartSpawnWritesNoSessionStart_spec_28_5_3, and tier-3 TestSubprocessSessionStartValidatesAgainstSchema_spec_28_5_3 call Start then Send untapped; they are the regression guard for the lazy path and must pass unchanged. ### [non-spec.21.review-mechanism.1]
FACT: The gateway's `adapterclient.Client.Attach` binds the stream with an envelope-free first `AttachRequest` (pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient/client.go:879-887), so the adapter's `Attach` subscribes to `rt.Output` (pkg/adapter/attach.go:60) before it writes any gateway message. Starting the hub reader at hub creation (CODE-6 item 18.2, r20) therefore drops no turn response on the gateway path, even though `Attach` writes a first-frame envelope before it subscribes (attach.go:53-60) and `linefanout.Hub.broadcast` drops lines with no subscriber (pkg/adapter/linefanout/linefanout.go:116-126). FACT: The bundled Basic-battery runtimes (echo, streaming-echo, delegation-echo, binary-minimal scaffold) handle a `message` synchronously in their frame loop. DECISION: no performance or failure-mode finding in non-spec round 26 — BECAUSE the r25 delta (CODE-6 item 16 paging plus `Concurrency`, the adapter `clock`/`now()` default, the spec-map rule move, the SuspendIdle retry-gate test) adds no per-unit write. This is not a finding. — EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md:400-402
FACT: an unlifted seal left by a coordinator crash between the seal and the suspend write delays held messages by at most one idle window. A refused `message` neither stamps the adapter clock nor resets the §6.2 clock, so the adopter's next `sweepIdle` attempt seals, checkpoints, and releases. This is no worse than the shipped idle expiry. — EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md:475 (client bullet "a message the runtime adapter writes"), :801; non-spec-changes.md:337 (Refusal: no write and no stamp)

### [non-spec.29.review-performance.1]
DECISION: no performance or failure-mode finding in non-spec round 29 — BECAUSE the r27 delta is only the tier-5 concurrent-pool drain test rewrite, and the 7c21ce84f delta's new hot paths stay within settled bounds: the llmproxy per-line `Stamp` coalesces at 1 s per session (sessionidle.go:178-192), `StampAt` runs only on a `sealed: false` answer (once per idle window per session), `beginToolCall` is one `s.mu` hold per call, and `admitResume` issues no COUNT while every cap is disabled — ALTERNATIVES: filing the synchronous `admitResume` in `ResumeBacklog` as a Tick stall during a primary partition (rejected: `Tick` already runs `List`/`Update` on the long-lived context with no per-tick deadline, watchdog.go:588-617, so no new class of stall); filing concurrent idle-suspension checkpoints as unbounded (rejected: the steady-state bound is about 11/s at Tier 3, already in Settled **Per-message and idle costs.**)
FACT: `Stamper.pruneLocked` scans the whole coalescing map on each non-coalesced `Stamp` once the map holds 4096 or more entries (sessionidle.go:210-221). That is O(n^2) per second per replica when n or more sessions stamp each second. FACT: The tenant-suspend drain force-terminates every non-terminal session, `suspended` included, so a podless `suspended` session cannot be backlog-resumed for a suspended tenant. §11.4 full revoke cancels the user's non-terminal sessions, and soft and hard disable deny only new sessions, so a resume needs no user-gate check. CODE-7's `admitResume` keys on `row.UserID`, the same column the count reads, so the resume check is no weaker than creation. The Subject-versus-body mismatch predates 0092. Do not file it against 0092. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/create.go:99-104, :241; pgstore.go:880-891
FACT: `beginToolCall` keeps the `callingSession` exclusivity gate, so a call is refused unless exactly one session resolves. The adapter has no per-method auth allowlist (only `coordinatorHoldAllowedMethods` and `credredact`), so the seal RPCs need no auth entry. EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/platformtoolprovider.go:69-76, pkg/adapter/runtimegeneration.go:162-170, pkg/adapter/holdstate.go:53-55
DECISION: Filed nothing. BECAUSE: under the security lens, every bound the delta touches is gateway-authoritative and fails closed. The cap COUNTs run on the primary and answer 500 on error. Active age is a Postgres column. The `idle_age_seconds` that SealSession returns feeds only a forward-only stamp, which a lying adapter could already obtain by answering not sealed. A runtime's `busy` affects only idleness, and `maxSessionAge` still bounds it. ALTERNATIVES: filing `IdleSuspendable`'s skip-on-resolve-error (a session whose runtime record is missing is never idle-reclaimed). It is a reclamation gap and not a security control, so a mechanism lens should look at it if anyone does.

### [non-spec.35.review-kubernetes.1]
FACT: The proposal adds no CRD field, status condition, finalizer, ownerReference, or webhook change; every new state lives in Postgres or Redis. FACT: The orphan-claim GC's active-session oracle is `GetActiveSlotsByPod`, which counts every non-terminal row naming the pod. A held-pod `suspended` row therefore protects its claim, and a podless row (after the release's guarded clear) leaves the claim to be drained on the next GC tick. Deleting a claim whose pod projects `claimed` drains the pod, so the release and failure paths fail closed. — EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/session/sessionstore/pgstore/pgstore.go:742-757; cmd/lenny-controller/main.go:180; spec/04_system-components.md:415

### [non-spec.35.review-performance.1]
FACT: a refused seal (`sealed == false`) costs one `SealSession` RPC plus one uncoalesced `StampAt` row write per idle window per session. The stamp is strictly forward: the row is over-idle (now - rowLAA >= W) and the adapter is not idle (now - adapterLA < W), so the stamp lands later than the row's value, and it uses durations only, so clock skew between gateway and pod does not matter. A busy or tool-calling session therefore re-arms once per W and does not churn every 5 s tick. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md CODE-6 item 4 **`SuspendIdle`.** step 1; pkg/gateway/session/sessionidle/sessionidle.go `persist` (forward-only Update).
FACT: `Stamper.persist` drops its Update error, so during a Postgres failover a refused seal's stamp is lost and the holder retries `SealSession` each 5 s watchdog tick until the primary returns. The RPC is bounded and causes no store churn. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/session/sessionidle/sessionidle.go persist `_, _ = s.store.Update`.
FACT: adapter default heartbeat interval is 30 s with a 10 s ack timeout, so the new per-entry monitors (CODE-6 item 18.3) add negligible pod-local load. EVIDENCE: cmd/lenny-adapter/main.go:225-230.
FACT: no current `pkg/adapter` path holds `s.mu` across `WriteEnvelope`, `Interrupt`, or `Checkpoint`, so the tap taking `s.mu` per runtime frame (item 18.1) cannot stall the hub reader behind runtime I/O. EVIDENCE: awk scan of pkg/adapter/*.go non-test files.
WATCHOUT: a seal left by a coordinator that crashed between step 1 and step 3 stays while the runtime keeps reporting activity, because a later attempt that gets `sealed == false` stamps and does not unseal. Messages then wait in the DLQ until the runtime goes idle for W and the adopter's attempt completes. This is the staged SPEC-5ab design ("A seal that its attempt does not lift stays until..."), so it is not a non-spec finding. EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md:801.

### [non-spec.37.review-reliability.1]

FACT: `sessionidle.Stamper.Stamp` is non-blocking. It coalesces to one write per second per session and persists in a goroutine under a 5 s timeout, and it drops failures. The CODE-6 item 5 per-chunk `flush` stamp therefore cannot stall an LLM stream during a Postgres failover. A dropped `StampAt` on the `SuspendIdle` not-sealed branch only means the next watchdog tick asks the adapter again, so it is not a stampede. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/session/sessionidle/sessionidle.go:178-192, :227-239
FACT: Client messages do not stamp `last_agent_activity_at`. Only agent-activity events published through `publishEvent` do, along with the LLM-proxy usage stamps. A sealed `running` session whose refused messages sit in the DLQ is therefore re-attempted by the next idle firing, and the client's sending does not hold it off. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/events.go:360-370, cmd/lenny-gateway/llmproxy_usage.go:316,:474
FACT: A held message stranded in the DLQ of a `running` session after a Lift or a checkpoint-failure unseal is spec-accepted. SPEC-5i **Delivery of held messages.** says it "waits for the next delivery point or the session's expiry". Do not file it as a reliability defect. EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md SPEC-5i **Delivery of held messages.** (the sentence "When no message arrives, the idle suspension ... deliver it, except while the idle suspension does not complete")
FACT: Runtime soft delete keeps `runtimestore.Get` answering, because pgstore `Get` has no `deleted_at` filter. As a result `IdleSuspendable`'s resolve error is transient only, and a deleted runtime does not leave an over-idle row skipped forever. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/runtime/runtimestore/pgstore/pgstore.go:282-293, :398-404
WATCHOUT: Each failure arm of `openRuntimeSession` releases the claim, so a second `session_start` on the same registry entry, which would find a stopped non-nil `entry.hb` and start no monitor, has no path in the tree. Before filing that as a missed monitor restart, confirm that a caller reuses the entry. EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/session.go:183-199, pkg/adapter/resume.go:171-181, pkg/adapter/sdkwarm.go:277-287

### [non-spec.37.review-security.1]
FACT: The round-37 delta adds only the wiring test for the llmproxy per-chunk stamp. `newLLMProxyServer` returns `&http.Server{Handler: proxyMux}` with no middleware wrapper, so asserting through `ServeMux.Handler` is feasible — EVIDENCE: cmd/lenny-gateway/llmproxy_server.go:33-60
DECISION: no security finding — BECAUSE every bound the delta touches comes from a trusted source. The per-chunk stamp keys on the gateway-held proxy-mode lease (TenantID and SessionID), and it fires only in proxy mode. A pod's `busy` or seal refusal can defer only idle suspension, which is a resource bound. Active-time `maxSessionAge` still accrues while the session is `running`. The cap counts are primary-pool Postgres and fail closed. The idle-suspension release takes the pool's normal session-end disposition, so recycle and scrub are unchanged — ALTERNATIVES: filing runtime-controlled `busy` as an attacker-influenceable bound was rejected, because idle suspension is not a security property and the age cap stays gateway-measured.

FACT: The gateway control gRPC server sets no server keepalive and `GracefulStop()` runs with no deadline, so a pod that dies without closing its stream is never observed and the resolved branch never calls `EndWait`. EVIDENCE: cmd/lenny-gateway/runserver.go (`w.gatewayCtrlSrv.GracefulStop()`); keepalive appears only on the client dial side.

### [spec.30.fix-design-G3.1]
DECISION: SPEC-5p2 item 1 (§9.2 **Elicitation Timeout Semantics:** item 6) becomes the one home of the paths on which a held resolution is not enqueued, by one sentence after "enqueues each resolution at most once." — BECAUSE the non-spec Edge cases bullet already accepts those losses and only the landing spec text promised otherwise — ALTERNATIVES: a durable reclaim (an `enqueued` column plus an `EndWait`-style sweep at restore commit or a leader re-check) lost: a new mechanism, and it still cannot tell a live child's wait from an ended one without the observation the losses lack.
DECISION: SPEC-5p2 item 2 is deleted, and SPEC-2d item 3 drops "no call is blocked on a pod and". The §29.3 row then says only who records the resolution; §9.2 item 6 alone says when it is enqueued. This closes the double delivery to a running child (finding 4) and the tool-use approvals enqueued as elicitation resolutions (finding 5) with one deletion.
FACT: an elicitation's interaction row is keyed to the resolver (root) session, and `Detail["originPod"]` names the raising session. The waiting `request_elicitation` handler polls `Interactions.Get` in Postgres, so a resolution that a non-coordinator replica records reaches a still-live child's call with no forward. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/mcptools_register.go:1600-1615; elicitation.go:140-145
FACT: the gateway's control gRPC server sets no server keepalive (the only keepalive is the gateway-to-adapter client dial), and shutdown calls `GracefulStop()` with no deadline. A pod that dies silently therefore leaves the handler waiting until `maxElicitationWait`, and a respond that arrives in that window returns into a dead stream without `EndWait`. EVIDENCE: cmd/lenny-gateway/runserver.go:222-224; cmd/lenny-gateway/pod_lifecycle.go:215
OPEN: the base §29.3 interaction-resolution row says the root's coordinator "resolves the pending ... elicitation the pod is blocked on". For a child's elicitation the blocked pod belongs to the child, and the code resolves it by Postgres polling rather than by a forward. This is a pre-existing spec wording gap and is not this proposal's edit.
WATCHOUT: do not re-add an enqueue clause to the §29.3 row, in any state-qualified or kind-qualified form. Item 6 is the home, and the row covers tool-use approvals too.
